ITQAN:v2p566/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r17.claim: نشرا is the plural of نشور.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p331/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p331/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p331/r8.claim: One Qur'anic sense of mercy is rain.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p331/r8.anchor: والسادس : المطر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف : ^ ( وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته ) ^

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r14.claim: A discourse on God's signs to humanity in verses 52–58 introduces extended accounts of earlier communities destroyed after rejecting their prophets.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r14.anchor: the various signs of God to humanity (vv. 52–58), which serves as an introduction to a lengthy segment

BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r1.claim: Bushran is a shortened form of bushur, plural of bashīr, meaning bearers of glad tidings.
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r1.anchor: تخفيف بشر بضمتين جمع بشير نحو رغيف ورغف ، أي : مبشرات.

BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r2.claim: The winds precede the rain: the east wind raises clouds, the north gathers them, the south drives rain from them, and the west disperses them; their directional names are explained.
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r2.anchor: فإن الصبا تثير السحاب والشمال تجمعه والجنوب تدره والدبور

BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas compares God’s winds carrying and working the clouds until rain falls to a man milking a she-camel or sheep.
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يرسل الله الرياح فتحمل السحاب فتمريه

BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r4.claim: The verse uses “mercy” to mean rain, so a saying about fleeing from mercy refers to fleeing from rain.
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r4.anchor: وفي الآية إطلاق الرحمة على المطر ، فقول : من قال إني أفر من الرحمة محمول على المطر

BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#3/r5.claim: The phrase “until it carries” marks the endpoint of the statement that God sends the winds.

BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r1.claim: Aqallat means the wind carried the cloud easily; carrying something with ease makes it seem light, hence its derivation from the sense of fewness.
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r1.anchor: أي : حملته ورفعته باليسر والسهولة بأن وجدته خفيفا قليلا يقال أقللت كذا ، أي : حملته بالسهولة

BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r2.claim: “Heavy” describes clouds laden with water; sahāb is a collective noun that can denote one cloud or many, so the adjective is plural in sense.
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r2.anchor: جمع ثقيل أي بالماء جمعه مع كونه وصفا للسحاب ، لأن السحاب اسم جنس

BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r3.claim: Sahāb means clouds moving through the sky.
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r3.anchor: والسحاب : هو الغيم الجاري في السماء

BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r4.claim: Sūqnāhu derives from driving; the pronoun refers to the clouds, singular in form to match the word’s grammatical form.
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r4.anchor: من السوق والضمير للسحاب والإفراد باعتبار اللفظ والمعنى بالفارسية

BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r5.claim: A dead land is a place without vegetation; balad can mean any inhabited or uninhabited location, while balda is a part of it and bilād its plural.
BURSEVI:v3p136#4/r5.anchor: {لبلد ميت} أي : لإحياء بلد لا نبات فيه والبلد يطلق على كل موضع

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the land, and the bāʾ marks water adhering to or being sent upon it.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r1.anchor: {فأنزلنا به المآء} أي : بالبلد والباء للإلصاق أي التصق إنزال الماء

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r2.claim: The next bāʾ means “by means of” that water; “all fruits” refers to every kind, with universality understood in the customary sense.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r2.anchor: {فأخرجنا به} أي : بسبب ذلك الماء {من كل الثمرات} أي : من كل أنواعها

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r3.claim: Resurrection is likened either to producing fruits or to reviving dead land: God will return souls to gathered bodily matter and restore powers and senses.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r3.anchor: الإشارة فيه إلى إخراج الثمرات أو إلى إحياء البلد الميت أي كما نحييه بإحداث القوة النباتية فيه

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r4.claim: The form tadhakkarūn drops one of two tāʾs and means “you remember,” teaching that the One who can do this can raise the dead without doubt.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r4.anchor: {لعلكم تذكرون} بطرح إحدى التاءين ، أي تتذكرون فتعلمون

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayra report that rain falls for forty days between the two blasts, bodies grow from graves as plants grow from water, receive souls, then awaken at the blast of resurrection.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبو هريرة : إذا مات الناس كلهم في النفخة الأولى مطرت السماء أربعين يوما

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r6.claim: In the inward reading, winds are care, cloud is guidance, water is love, and its fruits are visions, unveilings, and spiritual perfections; God raises dead hearts from the graves of breasts.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r6.anchor: والإشارة في الآية : أن الرياح رياح العناية ، والسحاب سحاب الهداية ، والماء ماء المحبة

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r7.claim: The lesson recalls the life of intimacy and nearness in the holy precincts.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r7.anchor: أي موتى القلوب من قبور الصدور لعلكم تذكرون ، أي : تذكرون أيام حياتكم

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r8.claim: Primordial divine care is the foundation and reaches servants in public and private; a story begins of a saint sent among polytheists, captured, and serving at a church faithfully.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r8.anchor: واعلم : أن العمدة هي العناية الأزلية ، وهي تصل إلى العباد في الخلا والملا حكي أنه قيل

BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r9.claim: The story continues that the saint was sold to a church servant, served honestly, then appeared to a sultan who had emptied the church to pray and answered that he was a Muslim like him.
BURSEVI:v3p136#5/r9.anchor: فأسره مشرك وباعه لخادم كنيسة فخدم فيها زمانا بالصدق ، فجاء السلطان يوما إلى الكنيسة

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the winds as heralds sent before divine mercy.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r2.claim: He reports Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Abu Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqub reading nushuran, while Ibn ʿAmir reads nushran, yielding the sense of spreading winds before mercy.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r2.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ebû Ca‘fer, Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde نُشُراً, İbn Âmir’de نُشْراً okunduğuna göre:

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r3.claim: The received bushran is the plural of bashir; nushur is the plural of nashir or manshur.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r4.claim: Nashr can mean spreading or dispersal, pleasant fragrance, and a gentle, pleasant wind that spreads clouds.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r4.anchor: “Nûn”un fethiyle “neşr” dahi neşretmek, yaymak ve tefrik etmek mânasına masdar olduğu gibi, râyiha-i tayyibe mânasına

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Kisaʾi read al-riha nashran, which Elmalılı renders as a wind sent in a state of spreading before mercy.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r5.anchor: İbn Kesîr, Hamza, Kisâî kıraatlerinde الرِّيحَ نَشْراً okunduğuna göre de “rahmetinin önünde neşr hâlinde rüzgâr gönderir.”

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r6.claim: Winds are not all good omens: some are warnings of punishment, alongside those that herald mercy.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r6.anchor: Hâsılı korkulacak hareketler, münzir olan rüzgârlar da vardır.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r7.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r7.claim: Ibn Umar reports eight kinds of wind, divided evenly between four winds of punishment and four of mercy.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r7.anchor: İbn Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâ’dan mervîdir ki riyâh sekiz nevi‘dir. Dördü azab, dördü rahmettir.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r8.claim: He names the four punishment winds as kasif, asif, sarsar, and aqim, and the four mercy winds as nashirat, mubashshirat, mursalat, and dhariyat.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r8.anchor: Azab olanlar: Kāsıf, âsıf, sarsar, akīm. Rahmet olanlar da nâşirât, mübeşşirât, mürselât, zâriyâttır.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r9.speaker: Prophet
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r9.claim: A Prophetic report says the Prophet was aided by the east wind, ʿAd was destroyed by the west wind, and the south wind is from Paradise.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r9.anchor: Bir hadîs-i nebevîde de şöyle vârid olmuştur: نُصِرْتُ بِال َّصبَا وَأُهْلِكَتْ عَادٌ بِال َّدبُورِ، وَالْجَنُوبُ مِنْ رِيحِ الْجَن َّةِ

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r10.speaker: Ka‘b
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r10.claim: Kaʿb is reported to say that if God withheld the wind for three days, most of the earth would stink.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r10.anchor: Hazret-i Ka‘b’dan da menkuldür ki Allah üç gün rüzgârı hapsetse ekser arz kokardı.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r11.claim: Because winds can warn and bring mercy, hope cannot be separated from fear, nor fear from hope.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r11.anchor: Bunun için ümit hafvtan, havf ümitten münfek olmamak lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r12.claim: Wind is moving air, with many regular or irregular kinds according to direction and qualities; four or eight directions are usually treated as basic.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r12.anchor: Sûret-i umûmiyede cihât nokta-i nazarından dört veya sekiz rüzgâr esas gibi mülâhaza olunur.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r13.claim: Wind is a specific movement of air, not its natural state; physical accounts relate its formation to changing heat and cold, whose balance God directly governs.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r13.anchor: harâret tabiatı ile burûdet tabiatı arasındaki gālibiyet ve mağlûbiyet nisbetlerinin tahvil ve tasrîfine râci‘dir

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r14.claim: Both regular and irregular winds are direct divine action; those who look for God's power only in miracles wrongly think only extraordinary winds are divine acts.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r14.anchor: Onun için kudret-i ilâhiyeyi yalnız hârikada aramak gafletinde bulunanlar, fi‘l-i ilâhî ancak fevka’l-‘âde rüzgârlardır zannederler.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r15.claim: The point is not merely that wind proves a first mover; its further features and relation to life, blessing, and rain also direct reflection.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r15.anchor: burada mevzû‘-i bahis yalnız muharrik-i evvel delîlini teşkil eden bu tahrik değildir.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r16.claim: The wind prepares and signals the coming rain before it occurs, thereby representing a message to human reason about a later divine act.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r16.anchor: kable’l-vukū‘iş‘âr eylemesi haysiyetine de bilhassa nazar-ı dikkat celb olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:7:57-58/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r17.claim: Winds sent before mercy resemble messengers or angels heralding the divine mercy that will arrive later.
ELMALILI:7:57-58/r17.anchor: tebşir eyleyen bir resul, bir melek misâli vardır.

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r1.claim: One benefit of wind is to gather and spread clouds, carrying them overhead to places in need of rain.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r1.anchor: bulutları derleyip toplamak ve yaymak ve yağmura muhtaç olan yerlere götürmek

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r2.claim: The verse stresses the striking fact that light air lifts heavy clouds, contrary to ordinary expectations about weight.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r2.anchor: hava hafif, bulutlar ise ağırdır. Hafifin ağırı kaldırması ise hilâf-ı tabiattır.

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r3.claim: Clouds are not merely water vapor: recent discovery showed them to consist of aggregated liquid water droplets, which are heavier than air.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r3.anchor: hâlinde olduğu ahîren fark edilmiş ve suyun ise havadan sakil olduğu mâlum bulunmuş

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r4.claim: An initial theory held that hollow, soap-bubble-like droplets contained trapped air hotter than the outside air and therefore floated.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r4.anchor: o su habbecikleri sabun köpüğü gibi mücevvef ve içlerinde hava mahbus olup bu hava hâriçteki havadan fazla bir derece-i harârette bulunduğundan hafif olarak üzerinde yüzüyor” denilmiş

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r5.claim: He says the hollow-bubble theory was refuted in favor of full droplets, each heavier than an equal volume of air.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r5.anchor: sonra bu nazariye cerh olunarak sehâbı terkib eden su habbeciklerinin içi boş değil, dolgun bulunduğu

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r6.claim: The accepted account holds that wind motion keeps the heavier droplets suspended and moving in the air, like grains of sand driven upward.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r6.anchor: her biri kendi hacmindeki havadan sakil olduğu hâlde aşağıdan rüzgârın tahrîkiyle kum tanelerinin yukarı çıkması gibi

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r7.claim: The two theories compare buoyant light objects such as balloons and ships with heavy objects such as birds and airplanes staying aloft; the phrase about heavy clouds points to the latter.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r7.anchor: Evvelkine göre balon ve gemi gibi hafifin sakil üzerinde duruşu, ikinciye göre de kuş ve tayyâre gibi sakīlin hafif üzerinde duruşudur

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r8.claim: Even if warm air makes the water droplets into tiny bubbles, it is more striking that moving air lifts heavy clouds while they retain their weight.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r8.anchor: daha ziyade câlib-i dikkat bir hâdisedir ki, bunda hareketin ehemmiyeti

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r9.claim: The verse's account of moving winds lifting heavy clouds is, for Elmalılı, a scientific miracle and decisive evidence for Muhammad's prophethood.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r9.anchor: risâlet-i Muhammediyenin delâil-i kat‘iyyesinden birisi olan bir mu‘cize-i ilmiye var demektir.

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r10.claim: He calls it a miracle whose truth human science recognized only after a thousand years.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r10.anchor: Bir mucize ki fenn-i beşer bunun sıdkına bin seneden sonra vâkıf olabilmiştir.

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r11.claim: God gives wind its force but does not leave it inert under fixed nature; the wording turns to God's will and sovereign command.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r11.anchor: Allah rüzgâra o kuvveti vermekle beraber onu onda atâlet kāidesi üzere bir tabiat istivâsıyla bırakmıyor.

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r12.claim: At the moment the winds lift the heavy clouds, God says that He drives the cloud toward a dead land.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r12.anchor: Biz o sehâbı ölü bir belde için sevk ederiz de

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r13.claim: God sends water down to that land and brings out every kind of fruit through it.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r13.anchor: o suyu o beldeye indiririz {فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِۦ مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ} ve o su ile her türlü meyveleri çıkarırız

ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r14.claim: The revival of a dead land demonstrates that the Lord who acts by motion and will can also raise the dead from their graves.
ELMALILI:7:57-58#2/r14.anchor: ölmüş bir beldeyi yeniden ihyâ etmeye kādir bulunan Rabbinizin ölüleri diriltebileceğinde şüphe yoktur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r1.claim: Repeated natural events are extraordinary signs of God's power that people overlook through familiarity; recurring renewal in nature indicates God's existence and sovereignty and the possibility of resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r1.anchor: tabiattaki sürekli canlanma ve yenilenme bir yandan onu canlandıran Allah’ın varlığına ve hükümranlığına, bir yandan da öldükten sonra yeniden dirilmenin mümkün olduğuna delâlet etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r2.claim: The verse's image of God reviving the dead from graves as he brings plants from dead soil is an especially striking addition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r2.anchor: âyetin sonuna, Allah’ın ölü topraktan türlü türlü canlı bitkiler çıkarması gibi kıyamet gününde ölüleri de kabirlerden diriltip çıkaracağı şeklinde bir bilginin eklenmesi özellikle ilgi çekicidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r3.claim: The Qur'an gives this knowledge to prompt reflection and moral awakening; it is a guide, not a natural science or astronomy textbook, and aims to ground belief and practice against deviation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r3.anchor: Çünkü Kur’an bir tabiat bilgisi veya astronomi kitabı değildir; onun temel gayesi insana rehber olmak; onu, akıl ve bilgi dünyasını sağlıklı temeller üzerine kurmaya

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r4.claim: The Qur'an's information, rules, and warnings aim to educate and develop humanity so people attain the honored status God intends for them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:57/r4.anchor: Kur’an’da verilen çeşitli konulara dair bilgilerin, düzenlemelerin, uyarıların asıl hedefi, insanlığın, Allah tarafından kendisine lâyık görülen seçkin konumuna ulaşacağı biçimde eğitilmesi ve geliştirilmesidir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.claim: Rain shows God’s mercy is near: when land is dry and people lose hope, He sends rain to drench it, so only He should be sought in hope or despair.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.anchor: It is He Who sends rain after the land gets dry and people lose hope and then drenches the earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.claim: As rain revives dead land, God will recreate human beings after death and decomposition.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p47/.anchor: God will re-create human beings after they die and decompose

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p48/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p48/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p48/.claim: The preceding discussion can produce disbelief and malice only in people with no potential; the coming verses should be read against this background.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p48/.anchor: produce scrubs and weeds of disbelief and malice in those who do not have the slightest potential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.claim: As he explains in Sūrah al-Anʿām, God could send bread directly, yet winds, clouds, rain, cultivation, and harvest reveal His creativity, governance, power, and wisdom in every part of creation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.anchor: a treasure of the signs of God’s creativity and governance and of His marvels of power and wisdom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.claim: The many transformations of a single object attract attention, letting people recognize God's signs and learn from them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p49/.anchor: A single object changes form and shape in so many ways in order to attract our attention

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: Here raḥmah means rain, a Qur’anic usage; the rain parable teaches that only God should be invoked in hope and fear because He alone sends life-giving rain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: connotes rain here. The Qur’ ān has used this word for rain on more than one occasion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: God brings monsoon winds that lift water-laden clouds and drive them to barren lands, demonstrating that rain comes only by His command.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: Not a single drop of rain, on which depends life of this whole world, can come down except at God’s behest.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: The same image appears in 42:28: God sends rain when people have lost hope and spreads His mercy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: In verse 28 of S ūrah Shūrā, the words are:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: Aqalla means to lift something as if it had no weight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: to lift something as if it has no weight.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: Saḥāb is the plural of saḥābah though singular in form, which explains the singular pronoun in saqnāhu.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: it is singular in form and shape. For this reason, a singular pronoun is used for it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: The preposition bi in fa-anzalnā bihi marks locus; the signs direct people to God’s power and mercy and to invoking Him alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: signifies locus. The verses direct our attention to His power and mercy and as a consequence to ask from Him alone in hope and fear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.claim: As rain revives dead land, God will raise all the dead; this visible power points to the Hereafter, and the signs aim to remind people of it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p55/.anchor: just as God through rain brings to life a dead stretch of land in a similar way He will bring all the dead back to life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.claim: These parable lessons allude in principle to the topics raised from the beginning of the sūrah through this point.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.anchor: all the topics that were raised in this sūrah from its beginning until here are, in principle, alluded to.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir reads singular الريح and reads نشرا with both nūn and shīn rounded.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير: وهو الذي يرسل الريح واحدة، (نشرا) مضمومة النون والشين.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r2.claim: Abu Amr and Nafi read plural الرياح with both nūn and shīn rounded in نشرا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو، ونافع: (الرياح) جماعة (نشرا) مضمومة النون والشين أيضا .

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r3.claim: Ibn Amir reads plural الرياح and gives نشرا a rounded nūn and vowelless shīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: (الرياح) جماعة (نشرا) مضمومة النون ساكنة الشين.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r4.speaker: عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r4.claim: Asim reads plural الرياح and بشرا with bāʾ and vowelless shīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: الرياح جماعة. بشرا بالباء. ساكنة الشين منونة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read singular الريح and نشرا with open nūn and vowelless shīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (الريح) على التوحيد، (نشرا) بفتح النون ساكنة الشين منونة .

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r6.claim: The noun الريح derives from a form whose root waw changes in the singular because of kasra; the small plural أرواح keeps waw because no change is required.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r6.anchor: اعلم أن الريح اسم على فعل، والعين منه واو، فانقلبت في الواحد للكسرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r7.claim: In the common plural رياح, waw becomes yāʾ after kasra; the following alif also favors the change because it resembles yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r7.anchor: وأما في الجمع الكثير فرياح، فانقلبت الواو ياء للكسرة التي قبلها

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r8.claim: A singular noun can denote a collective and take plural sense, as in الدينار والدرهم and 103:2 followed by the exception in 103:3; thus singular الريح can carry collective meaning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r8.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون (الريح) على لفظ الواحد، ويراد بها الكثرة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r9.claim: A poetic example describes one feminine subject with the plural numeral and plural color, supporting singular-form collective usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p31#2/r9.anchor:
وقد قال:
فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir’s singular الريح with plural نشرا is grammatical by meaning because the singular denotes a collective; nevertheless, plural الرياح with plural نشرا is preferable by agreement in form, reinforced by الرياح مبشرات.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r1.anchor: وقول من جمع الريح، إذا وصفها بالجميع الذي هو (نشرا) أحسن

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r2.speaker: ذو الرمة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r2.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses أرواح as the low-count plural of ريح, with waw retained.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r2.anchor:
قول ذي الرمة :
إذا هبت الأرواح من نحو جانب ... به آل مي هاج شوقي هبوبها

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r3.claim: The plural أرواح is not like عيد وأعياد because the latter has an obligatory sound substitution, while الريح does not.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r3.anchor: وليس ذلك كعيد وأعياد، لأن هذا بدل لازم، وليس البدل في الريح كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that a wind be made plural (رياح) rather than singular (ريح); the author explains that Quranic plural winds usually bring rain and mercy, while destructive winds are singular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r4.anchor: جاء في الحديث من أن النبي، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يقول إذا هبت ريح: «اللهم اجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا»

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses نشرا as winds dispersed from every direction.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r5.anchor: أبو عبيدة : (نشرا) أي متفرقة من كل جانب،

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r6.claim: Abu Zayd says أنشر الله الريح means God sent the wind forth and sent it as نشرًا after death.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r6.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: قد أنشر الله الريح إنشارا، إذا بعثها، وقد أرسلها نشرا بعد الموت.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r7.claim: Al-Farisi explains أنشر الله الريح as giving it life, so the wind نشرَت means that it lived; he cites al-Murar al-Fuqasi as evidence.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p33/r7.anchor: أنشر الله الريح إنشارا مثل أحياها، فنشرت هي، أي: حييت، والدليل على أن إنشار الريح إحياؤها قول المرار الفقعسي

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:4#1/r1.claim: The standard Form IV imperfect indicative presents sending the winds as ongoing divine action.
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:4#1/r1.anchor: ongoing divine action of sending winds

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:5#1/r1.claim: The singular rīḥ replaces plural riyāḥ, shifting from multiple beneficial winds to one wind entity.
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:5#1/r1.anchor: shifts from multiple beneficial winds to a single wind entity

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#1/r1.claim: The dotting variant gives n-sh-r, spreading or scattering, and describes winds as spreading agents rather than heralds.

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#2/r1.claim: With fatḥa, nashran is an active verbal noun of n-sh-r, depicting winds as actively spreading.
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#2/r1.anchor: Vowel shift to fatḥa: active verbal noun of n-sh-r

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#3/r1.claim: Nushuran is a plural of nashūr or nashūra, presenting winds as multiple spreading or reviving agents.
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:6#3/r1.anchor: winds as multiple agents of revival

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:18#1/r1.claim: The contracted mayt can mean already dead, while full mayyit can mean destined to die; the reading shifts the land's death from process to state.
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:18#1/r1.anchor: The variant shifts the land's death from process to state

QIRAAT-ER:7:57:34#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:34#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:34#1/r1.claim: Full assimilation of tāʾ into dhāl produces a heavier consonant cluster that emphasizes the effort of remembering.
QIRAAT-ER:7:57:34#1/r1.anchor: heavier consonant cluster emphasizes the effort of remembering

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p75/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p75/r14.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p75/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says مطر is used for merciful rain and أمطر for punishment; Abū Ḥayyān counters that both verbs are transitive and cites the people of ʿĀd calling their expected mercy a cloud that would rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p75/r14.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد يقال في الرحمة مطر وفي العذاب أمطر وهذا معارض بقوله هذا عارض ممطرنا فإنهم لم يريدوا إلا الرحمة وكلاهما متعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r1.claim: After signs of God's power and knowledge in the upper world, the passage presents signs in the lower world, including wind, clouds, rain, minerals, plants, and animals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى الدلائل على كمال إلهيته وقدرته وعلمه من العالم العلوي أتبعهما بالدلائل من العالم السفلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r2.claim: Rain produces plant growth, and the two verses also establish resurrection, bringing together the beginning and return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r2.anchor: ويترتب على نزول المطر أحوال النبات وذلك هو المذكور في الآية وانجر مع ذلك الدلالة على صحة الحشر والنشر البعث والقيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r3.claim: The relative clauses in إن ربكم الله الذي and وهو الذي signal something already known and established to the hearer; the wording is not إن ربكم خلق or وهو يرسل الرياح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r3.anchor: وجعل الخبر موصولا في أن ربكم الله الذي وفي وهو الذي دلالة على كون ذلك معهودا عند السامع مفروغا من تحقق النسبة فيه والعلم به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r4.claim: One plural reading of الرياح نشرا takes نشرا as a plural of ناشر, meaning winds that spread, by analogy with forms like لابن and تامر; this plural is rare.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r4.anchor: وقرأ الرياح نشرا جمعين وبضم الشين جمع ناشر على النسب أي ذات نشر من الطي كلابن وتامر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r5.claim: The same vocalization may derive from نشور meaning revived, or be the regular plural نشور like صبور وصبر; he rejects deriving it from passive-participial نشور because that pattern is nonproductive and does not pluralize on فعل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r5.anchor: أو نشور من الحياة أو جمع نشور كصبور وصبر وهو جمع مقيس لا جمع نشور بمعنى منشور خلافا لمن أجاز ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r6.speaker: الحسن والسلمي وأبو رجاء والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وعيسى بن عمر وأبو يحيى وأبو نوفل ونافع وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r6.claim: These readers are named for the preceding reading with ḍamma on the shīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r6.anchor: الحسن والسلمي وأبو رجاء واختلف عنهم والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وعيسى بن عمر وأبو يحيى وأبو نوفل الأعرابيان ونافع وأبو عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r7.speaker: عبد الله وابن عباس وزر وابن وثاب والنخعي وطلحة بن مصرف والأعمش ومسروق وابن عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r7.claim: These readers use the same plural reading but with a sukūn on the shīn to lighten the ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r7.anchor: وقرأ كذلك جمعا إلا أنهم سكنوا الشين تخفيفا من الضم كرسل عبد الله وابن عباس وزر وابن وثاب والنخعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r8.speaker: مسروق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r8.claim: Masrūq is reported to read نشرا with fatḥ on both letters; it is a collective noun like غيب or نشء.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r8.anchor: وقرأ نشرا بفتح النون والشين مسروق فيما حكى عنه أبو الفتح وهو اسم جمع كغيب ونشىء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r9.speaker: ابن كثير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads الريح in the singular and نشرا with ḍamma; نشرا can be a plural describing a generic singular or a singular adjective like ناقة سرح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير الريح مفردا نشرا بالنون وضمها وضم الشين فاحتمل نشرا أن يكون جمعا حالا من المفرد لأنه أريد به الجنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r10.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read نشرا with fatḥ on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn, as a verbal noun for spreading in contrast to folding or for reviving the dead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p76/r10.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي نشرا بفتح النون وسكون الشين مصدرا كنشر خلاف طوى أو كنشر بمعنى حيي من قولهم أنشر الله الموتى فنشروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Sulami, and Ibn Abi ʿAblah read riyaah and bishran with damma on bāʾ and shīn, a plural of bashīra; this form is also reported from ʿAsim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r1.anchor: وقرأ الرياح جمعا ابن عباس والسلمي وابن أبي عبلة بشرا بضم الباء والشين ورويت عن عاصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r2.claim: ʿAsim also reads bishran with damma on bāʾ but sukūn on shīn, easing the pronunciation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم كذلك إلا أنه سكن الشين تخفيفا من الضم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r3.claim: Al-Sulami, also reported from ʿAsim, reads bishran with fatḥa on bāʾ and sukūn on shīn as a verbal noun of the shortened verb bashshara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r3.anchor: وقرأ السلمي أيضا بشرا بفتح الباء وسكون الشين وهو مصدر بشر المخفف ورويت عن عاصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa and Ibn Qutayb read bushrā with a shortened alif, treating it as a verbal noun like رجعى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميقع وابن قطيب بشرى بألف مقصورة كرجعى وهو مصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r5.claim: The eight readings divide into four with nūn and four with bāʾ; their forms make bushran a circumstantial modifier of the object or, for some verbal-noun forms, potentially of the subject as well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r5.anchor: فهذه ثماني قراءات أربعة في النون وأربع في الباء فمن قرأ بالباء جمعا أو مصدرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r6.claim: Sending the winds means releasing or spreading them; their spreading contrasts with folding and also evokes life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r6.anchor: لأن إرسالها هو إطلاقها وهو بمعنى النشر فكأنه قيل ينشر الرياح نشرا ووصف الريح بالنشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r7.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains al-nashr as winds dispersed in different directions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: في النشر إنها المتفرقة في الوجوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r8.speaker: الشاعر (غير مسمى)
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r8.claim: An unnamed poet describes the southern wind reviving the water with its breeze; the gloss says al-rayda and al-murīd mean wind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r8.anchor: وقال الشاعر في وصف الريح بالإحياء والموت: وهبت له ريح الجنوب وأحييت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r9.speaker: الشاعر (غير مسمى)
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r9.claim: A second unnamed poet wishes the wind would die so he can sit and rest, illustrating the wind's life and death imagery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r9.anchor: وقال الآخر: إني لأرجو أن تموت الريح ... فأقعد اليوم وأستريح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r10.claim: Between the hands of His mercy means before His favor, namely rain, one of the greatest blessings in its effects; the human expression is metaphorical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r10.anchor: ومعنى بين يدي رحمته أمام نعمته وهو المطر الذي هو من أجل النعم وأحسنها أثرا والتعيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r11.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r11.claim: Al-Kirmani explains the present يرسل here by the preceding future-oriented دعوه خوفا وطمعا; the past أرسل in al-Furqan, Fatir, and al-Rum fits their surrounding past contexts, while al-Rum's other wording follows a future context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77/r11.anchor: قال الكرماني: قال هنا يرسل لأن قبل ذلك وادعوه خوفا وطمعا فهما في المستقبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r1.claim: The clause marks the endpoint of sending the winds: they herald rain and carry clouds until those clouds are borne toward a dead land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r1.anchor: هذه غاية لإرسال الرياح والمعنى أنه تعالى يرسل الرياح مبشرات أو مبشرات إلى سوق السحاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r2.claim: Sahab is a collective noun with a feminine singular form; it may be masculine or feminine and may take plural agreement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r2.anchor: والسحاب اسم جنس بينه وبين مفرده تاء التأنيث فيذكر كقوله والسحاب المسخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r3.claim: The masculine pronoun in سقناه follows the lexical form sahab, while the first-person plural magnifies God's immense favor in directing the clouds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r3.anchor: ونسب السوق إليه تعالى بنون العظمة التفاتا لما فيه من عظيم المنة وذكر الضمير في سقناه رعيا للفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r4.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi describes winds drawing clouds from the meeting of sky and earth, spreading them in the sky; heaven opens, water runs onto the clouds, and they then rain. The author says this detail is not established from the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي يرسل تعالى الرياح فتأتي السحاب من بين الخافقين طرف السماء والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r5.speaker: أهل الحق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r5.claim: The people of truth hold that God alone subjects and directs the winds as He wills and decrees, with no partner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r5.anchor: ومذهب أهل الحق أن الله تعالى هو الذي يسخر الرياح ويصرفها حيث أراد بمشيئته وتقديره لا مشارك له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r6.claim: The author says al-Razi refuted the philosophers' account of how winds arise on four grounds and also refuted the astrologers' account, concluding that God is their mover by rational proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r6.anchor: وللفلاسفة كيفية في حصول الرياح ذكرها أبو عبد الله الرازي وأبطلها من وجوه أربعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r7.speaker: ابن عمران
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿImran classifies four winds as punishment—qāṣif, ʿāṣif, ṣarṣar, and ʿaqīm—and four as mercy—nashirāt, mubashshirāt, mursalāt, and dhāriyāt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عمران الرياح ثمان أربع منها عذاب وهي: القاصف والعاصف والصرصر والعقيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r8.claim: The author takes the lām in li-balad as a lām of conveyance, meaning the rain is delivered to the land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r8.anchor: واللام في لبلد عندي لام التبليغ كقولك قلت لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the lām as causal, meaning the winds drive clouds for the sake of a land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لأجل بلد فجعل اللام لام العلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r10.claim: The author sees little apparent difference between conveyance and cause: saying one drove wealth for someone entails its delivery, unlike driving it for someone's sake, which need not reach that person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r10.anchor: ولا يظهر فرق بين قولك سقت لك مالا وسقت لأجلك مالا فإن الأول معناه أوصلته لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r11.claim: Calling the land dead is a fitting metaphor for barrenness and lack of growth, like a body without life; the land is singled out as the place where people gather and settle and where mercy appears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r11.anchor: ووصف البلد بالموت استعارة حسنة لجدبه وعدم نباته كأنه من حيث عدم الانتفاع به كالجسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r12.claim: Yasin uses the general phrase dead earth because it highlights resurrection through signs of God's power, including night and the carrying of descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r12.anchor: ولما كان في سورة يس المقصد إظهار الآيات العظيمة الدالة على البعث جاء التركيب باللفظ العام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r13.claim: ʿAsim, Abu ʿAmr, and al-Aʿmash read the yāʾ in mayyit with sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p77#2/r13.anchor: وسكن ياء الميت عاصم وأبو عمرو والأعمش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r1.claim: In fa-anzalna bihi al-maʾ, the bāʾ is locative and the pronoun refers to the nearest antecedent, the dead land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن الباء ظرفية والضمير عائد على بلد ميت أي فأنزلنا فيه الماء وهو أقرب مذكور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r2.claim: Other readings of the pronoun take the bāʾ as causal and refer it to the clouds, or refer it to the implied act of driving the clouds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r2.anchor:
وقيل الباء سببية والضمير
عائد على السحاب. وقيل عائد على المصدر المفهوم من سقناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r3.claim: The author rejects taking the pronoun back to an implied verbal noun, since a suitable expressed antecedent is already present.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r3.anchor: والثالث ضعيف لأنه عائد على غير مذكور مع وجود المذكور وصلاحيته للعود عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r4.claim: A further proposal makes the bāʾ mean min and the pronoun refer to clouds, as in يشرب بها; the author says this is poor because it forces one preposition to carry another's sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r4.anchor: وقيل: عائد على السحاب والباء بمعنى من أي فأنزلنا منه الماء كقوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r5.claim: The pronoun in the second bihi of fa-akhrajna bihi has the same disputed antecedents; one proposal shifts the first pronoun to clouds and the second to the land without an intervening separator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r5.anchor: فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات الخلاف في به كالخلاف السابق في به.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r6.claim: Bringing out fruit is a visible analogue for bringing the dead from their graves alive to the gathering, so people should recall their promised resurrection from the renewal of plants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r6.anchor: أي مثل هذا الإخراج نخرج الموتى من قبورهم أحياء إلى الحشر لعلكم تذكرون بإخراج الثمرات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r7.speaker: محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r7.claim: Razin al-ʿUqayli asks the Prophet how God will restore creation and what sign is in creation; the Prophet points to a dry valley later seen green as God's sign.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r7.anchor: خرج البيهقي وغيره عن رزين العقيلي قال قلت: يا رسول الله كيف يعيد الله الخلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r8.claim: The author leaves two possible scopes for the simile: the general act of bringing forth, with fruits proving God's power to raise the dead, or the same manner of resurrection through rain that revives the dead land.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r8.anchor: وهل التشبيه في مطلق الإخراج ودلالة إخراج الثمرات على القدرة في إخراج الأموات أم في كيفية الإخراج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that life-water from beneath the Throne rains for forty years, the dead grow like crops, receive spirits, sleep, then rise at the second trumpet and hear that this is the Merciful's promise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p78/r9.anchor: وقد روي عن أبي هريرة أنه يمطر عليهم من ماء تحت العرش يقال له ماء الحيوان أربعين سنة

QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r10.claim: Signs of nearness arrive before proximity, like a breeze reaching the inner senses; signs of turning away bring inner constriction and estrangement before the breeze of union follows.
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r10.anchor: تباشير القرب تتقدم فيتأدى نسيمه إلى مشام الأسرار ، وكذلك آثار الإعراض تتقدم فتوجد ظلمة القبض في الباطن

QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r11.speaker: قائلهم
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r11.claim: A cited poem compares sensing fate approaching one's need to feeling a breeze from the beloved's hands.
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r11.anchor: وفي قريب منه قال قائلهم : ولقد تشممت القضاء لحاجتي . . . فإذا له من راحتيك نسيم

QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r12.claim: A heartbroken, withered seeker is renewed by nearness: union makes the once-dried state green and fresh again, like a dead person brought back to life.
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r12.anchor: فيأتيه القرب فيعود عود وصاله بعد الذبول طريا ، ويصير دارس حاله عقيب السقوط نديا

QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r13.speaker: بعضهم
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r13.claim: A cited poem depicts a person dressed in a shroud whose spirit returns to the body and whose union restores birth.
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r13.anchor: كما قال بعضهم : كنا كمن ألبس أكفانه . . . وقرب النعش من اللحد

QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r14.claim: A pure root produces a sound branch: a pure heart yields good outward deeds, whereas a corrupt interior produces the opposite state.
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r14.anchor: إذا زكا الأصل نما الفرع ، وإن خبث الجوهر لم يطب ما تحلل منه

QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r15.claim: The Prophet delivered the message, but revealed blessings did not benefit those whose allotted share was misery; effort cannot help someone deprived by divine allotment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p337/r15.anchor: بلغ الرسالة فلم ينجع فيهم ما أظهر من الآلاء ، لأن محروم القسمة لا ينفعه مجهود الحيلة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r1.claim: The sentence about sending winds connects either to the preceding sentence or to the discourse on creating the heavens and earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r1.anchor: عطف على الجملة السابقة أو على حديث خلق السموات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r2.claim: They read الريح in the singular, which can carry a collective sense and refer to many winds.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي ( الريح ) على الوحدة وهو متحمل لمعنى الجنسية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r3.claim: The supplication asking God to make them winds rather than wind is framed according to the majority reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r3.anchor: وخبر اللهم اجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا مخرج على قراءة الأكثرين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r4.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r4.claim: Asim reads بشرا with ḍamma on ب and a light, vowelless ش; it is a plural of بشير like نذر and means bringers of good tidings.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r4.anchor: وهي قراءة عاصم وروي عنه أيضا بشرا على الاصل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r5.claim: A reported reading from Asim also has بشرا according to its original form.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r5.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا بشرا على الاصل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r6.claim: A reading with fatḥa on ب treats the word as a verbal noun meaning heralding or bearing good news.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r6.anchor: وقريء بفتح الباء على أنه مصدر بشره بالتخفيف بمعنى بشره المشدد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r7.claim: Another reading, بشرى, is like حبلى and is also a verbal noun derived from giving good news.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r7.anchor: وقريء ( بشرى ) كحبلى وهو مصدر أيضا من البشارة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r8.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r8.claim: They read نشرا with ḍamma on ن and ش, a plural of نشور meaning spreading or spreading out; fuʿūl regularly forms such plurals when it means an active agent.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة ( نشرا ) بضم النون والشين جمع نشور بفتح النون بمعنى ناشر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r9.speaker: الحواشي الشهابية
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r9.claim: The glosses say ناشر may be relational to spreading, the opposite of folding, or to resurrection, since wind is described as dead and alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r9.anchor: قيل : هو على النسب إما إلى النشر ضد الطي وإما إلى النشور بمعنى الاحياء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r10.claim: A poetic line speaks of the wind dying, and another writer jokes in intense heat that the garden breeze has died and is ill.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r10.anchor: إني لأرجو أن تموت الريح فاقعد اليوم وأستريح

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r11.claim: Another explanation makes ناشر the active participle of a dead thing rising when God raises it, so it means one that revives or raises the dead.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : هو فاعل من نشر مطاوع أنشر الله تعالى الميت فنشر وهو ناشر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r12.claim: A further poetic line uses الناشر for the dead person who rises, supporting the resurrection sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r12.anchor: حتى يقول الناس مما رأوا يا عجبا للميت الناشر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r13.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r13.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows فعول to mean a passive participle here, like رسول/رسل, but the singular and plural are both rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : فعول هنا بمعنى مفعول كرسول ورسل وقد جوز ذلك أبو البقاء إلا أنه نادر مفرده وجمعه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r14.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r14.claim: Ibn Amir reads نشرا with ḍamma on ن and sukūn on ش wherever the form occurs; lightening this fuʿl form is regular.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ( نشرا ) بضم النون وسكون الشين حيث وقع والتخفيف في فعل مطرد

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r15.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r15.claim: They read نشرا with fatḥa on ن wherever it occurs, as a verbal noun used adverbially or as an absolute object because sending and spreading are close in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( نشرا ) بفتح النون حيث وقع على أنه مصدر في موقع الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r16.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r16.claim: The phrase بين يدي رحمته means before His mercy, and this use is metaphorical, as Abu Bakr al-Anbari transmits.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r16.anchor: أي قدام رحمته وهو من المجاز كما نقل عن أبي بكر الانباري

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r17.speaker: غالب المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r17.claim: Most exegetes understand God's mercy here as rain, named for the benefits that ordinarily follow it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r17.anchor: والمراد بالرحمة كما ذهب اليه غالب المفسرين المطر وسمي رحمة لما يترتب عليه بحسب جري العادة من المنافع

ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r18.claim: Calling rain mercy is figurative if the general word is used specifically, but literal if rain is treated as one instance of the general meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p144#2/r18.anchor: إن كان من حيث خصوصه مجاز لكونه استعمال اللفظ في غير ما وضع له

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r1.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r1.claim: Al-Shihab claims that some linguists establish rain as one of the meanings of mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r1.anchor: وادعى الشهاب اثبات بعض أهل اللغة كون المطر من معاني الرحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r2.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r2.claim: Ibn Hisham says he finds no lexicographer listing rain under mercy; the author replies that failure to find evidence does not prove it absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r2.anchor: وقول ابن هشام في رسالته التي ألفها في بيان وجه تذكير ( قريب ) المار عن قريب إنا لا نجد أهل اللغة حيث يتكلمون على الرحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r3.claim: An affirmative attestation outweighs a negative one, and someone who has retained evidence can inform one who has not.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r3.anchor: قصارى ما فيه عدم الوجدان وهو لا يستدعي عدم الوجود ومما اشتهر أن المثبت مقدم على النافي ومن حفظ حجة على من لم يحفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r4.claim: The context clearly supports taking mercy here to mean rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r4.anchor: والقام ظاهر في إرادة هذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r5.claim: A common account says the east wind stirs clouds, the north gathers them, the south brings rain, and the west disperses them; these are four familiar Arab winds.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r5.anchor: إن الصبا تثير السحاب والشمال تجمعه ولاجنوب يدره والدبور تفرقه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports eight winds: four of punishment, and four of mercy named the spreaders, bearers of good news, sent ones, and scatterers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن الرياح ثمانية أربع منها عذاب وهي القاصف والعاصف

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r7.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says that if God withheld wind for three days, most people on earth would become foul-smelling.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r7.anchor: وعن كعب الاحبار لو حبس الله تعالى الريح عن عباده ثلاث أيام لأنتن أكثر أهل الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r8.claim: Some transmitted accounts say God filled the world with air and that holding it back for an hour would make everything between heaven and earth foul-smelling.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r8.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن الله تعالى خلق العالم وملأه هواء ولو أمسك الهواء ساعة لأنتن ما بين السماء والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r9.speaker: غير واحد من العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r9.claim: Several scholars say it is disliked to curse the wind.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r9.anchor: وذكر غير واحد من العلماء أنه يكره سب الريح

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r10.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r10.claim: The Prophet says wind comes from God's spirit and brings mercy and punishment; people should not curse it, but ask God for its good and seek refuge from its evil. Abu Hurayra reports this after a wind struck people on the Mecca route while Umar was on pilgrimage and asking about its meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r10.anchor: فاني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : الريح من روح الله تعالى تأتي بالرحمة وتأتي بالعذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r11.claim: The hadith does not conflict with the verse: the verse does not say winds are sent only before mercy; if read that way, it describes the usual case since wind punishment is rare.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r11.anchor: إذ ليس فيها أنه سبحانه لايرسلها إلا بين يدي الرحمة ولئن سلم فهو خارج مجرى الغالب فان العذاب بالريح نادر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r12.claim: Another explanation says the report describes wind bringing mercy and punishment, not that every wind is sent ahead of either one.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r12.anchor: وقيل : ما في الخبر إنما هو الايتاء بالرحمة والايتاء بالعذاب لا الارسال بين يدي كل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r13.claim: The clause حتى إذا أقلت marks the endpoint of يرسل; iqlāl literally derives from making or deeming something small and came to mean carrying because a bearer regards the load as small.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r13.anchor: غاية لقوله سبحانه ( يرسل ) والاقلال كما في جمع البيان حمل الشيء بأسره واشتقاقه من القلة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r14.claim: سحاب is named for drifting through the air; it is a collective noun distinguished from its individual unit by ة and can be masculine or feminine, with singular or plural modifiers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p145/r14.anchor: سمي بذلك لانسحابه في الهواء وهو اسم جنس جمعي يفرق بينه وبين واحده بالتاء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r1.speaker: الجوهري وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r1.claim: Some language authorities call سحاب a plural; accordingly, Arabic varies in the number of its modifiers and pronouns, and its plural forms include سحب and سحائب.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r1.anchor: وأهل اللغة كالجوهري وغيره تسميه جمعا فلذا روعي فيه الوجهان في وصفه وضميره

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r2.claim: The clouds are heavy because of the water they contain; ثقال is the opposite of lightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r2.anchor: من الثقل كعنب ضد الخفة يقال : ثقل ككرم ثقلا وثقالة فهو ثقيل وثقل السحاب بما فيه من الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r3.claim: The lām in لبلد may mean for the land's benefit, to revive it, or to water it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r3.anchor: أي لأجله ومنفعته أو لاحيائه أو لسقيه كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r4.claim: Al-Bahr analyzes the lām as marking the recipient of communication, as in قلت لك; delivering something to someone entails arrival, while doing something for their sake does not.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r4.anchor: وفي البحر أن اللام للتبليغ كما في قلت لك وفرق بين سقت لك مالا وسقت لأجلك مالا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r5.claim: A land or country can be any place on earth, inhabited or not, empty or settled; بلد also means an individual town, while بلدة can mean a desert.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r5.anchor: والبلد كما قال الليث كل موضع في الأرض عامر أو غير عامر خال أو مسكون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r6.speaker: الأعشى
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r6.claim: Al-A'sha's line describes a desolate desert place as a shield's back, illustrating بلدة as a wilderness.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r6.anchor: وتطلق البلدة على المفازة ومنه قول الاعشى : وبلدة مثل ظهر الترس موحشة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r7.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r7.claim: They take the pronoun in فأنزلنا به to refer to the land or to the cloud; other suggestions refer it to the driving of the cloud or to the winds.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r7.anchor: أي بالبلد أو السحاب كما قال الزجاج وابن الانباري أو بالسوق أو الرياح كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r8.claim: The pronoun most likely returns to the water because it is closest in wording and meaning and matches the parallel clauses, though anaphoric pronouns need not always return to the same noun when context supports it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r8.anchor: وهو الظاهر لقربه لفظا ومعنى ومطابقة النظائر وانفكاك الضمائر لابأس به إذا قام الدليل عليه وحسن الملاءمة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r9.claim: If the pronoun refers to land, the two prepositions can be read as attachment and location respectively; a locative reading for the first is also possible. For other antecedents, the باء expresses cause, near or remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146/r9.anchor: وإذا كان للبلد فالباء للظرفية في الثاني وللالصاق في الاول لأن الانزال ليس في البلد بل المنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r1.claim: من كل الثمرات means every kind of fruit, not an exhaustive claim that every individual fruit is present; this makes God's power clearer.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r1.anchor: أي من كل انواعها لأن الاستغراق غير مراد ولا واقع وهذا أبلغ في اظهار القدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the totality as customary or contextually limited.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r3.claim: The apparent meaning is abundance rather than exhaustive totality.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r4.claim: Some allow من to be partitive or to specify the kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r4.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن تكون ( من ) للتبعيض وأن تكون لتبيين الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r5.claim: The comparison in كذلك نخرج الموتى may refer either to bringing out fruits or to reviving the dead land; as God revives land with growth, He raises the dead by returning souls to their bodily matter and restoring powers and senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r5.anchor: اشارة إلى اخراج الثمرات أو إلى احياء البلد الميت أي كما نحييه باحداث القوى النامية فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r6.claim: The passage is said to indicate both accounts of bodily resurrection: creating and enlivening a body after nonexistence, or reassembling its parts in their former pattern and then enlivening it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r6.anchor: وهو اشارة كما قيل إلى طريقي القائلين بالمعاد الجسماني وهما ايجاد البدن بعد عدمه ثم احياؤه وضم بعض اجزائه إلى بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r7.claim: The first account is more apparent: the comparison is between bringing forth both things from nonexistence; the second requires importing revival and reassembly, which are absent from the comparison on the other side.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r7.anchor: المتبادر من الآية كون التشبيه بين الاخراجين من كتم العدم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r8.claim: There is no valid proof that creation from nonexistence is impossible; transmitted evidence supports both routes, so either is possible if bodily resurrection is accepted, though fruits may have some prior basis and raising the dead by the first route is technically restoration.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r8.anchor: وأنت تعلم أنه لا مانع من الاخراج من كتم العدم وادلة استحالة ذلك مما لاتقوم على ساق وقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r9.speaker: الخازن
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r9.claim: Al-Khazin reports the view that God grows plants through rain and raises the dead through rain as well; Abu Hurayra and Ibn Abbas report that after the first trumpet, rain called the water of life falls for forty years, bodies grow like plants, receive their spirits, sleep in their graves, then rise at the second trumpet and recognize sleep's taste before the caller answers them with 36:52.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r9.anchor: فقد روي عن أبي هريرة وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهم أن الناس إذا ماتوا في النفخة الاولى أمطر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r10.claim: Mujahid says that when God wills to raise the dead, He rains until the earth splits open, then sends souls back to their bodies; thus He revives the dead by rain just as He revives the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r10.anchor: وأخرج غير واحد عن مجاهد أنه إذا أراد الله تعالى أن يخرج الموتى أمطر السماء حتى تشقق عنهم الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r11.claim: Another view says the comparison concerns only the basic fact of revival, without specifying how; believers should affirm it without investigating the manner, since God does what He wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p146#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : إنما وقع التشبيه بأصل الاحياء من غير اعتبار كيفية فيجب الايمان به ولا يلزمنا البحث عن الكيفية

ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r1.claim: The lesson is that whoever can do this is plainly able to do that as well, referring to resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r1.anchor: فتعلمون أن من قدر على ذلك فهو قادر على هذا من غير شبهة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r2.claim: The underlying form is تتذكرون, with one of the two ت letters deleted.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r3.claim: The address is said to be to observers generally or, alternatively, to those who deny resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p147/r3.anchor: والخطاب قيل : للنظار مطلقا وقيل : لمنكري البعث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim reads بشرا with bāʾ and a rounded, still shīn, meaning winds that announce rain, as in 30:46.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم "بشرا" بالباء وضمها وسكون الشين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read نشرا with open nūn, meaning a gentle, pleasant wind, as in 77:3.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي "نشرا" بالنون وفتحها، وهي الريح الطيبة اللينة، قال الله تعالى] : (1) (والناشرات نشرا) [المرسلات-3] ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads نشرا with rounded nūn and still shīn; others round both letters, as the plural of نشور, like صبور/صبر and رسول/رسل, for winds blowing from every direction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بضم النون وسكون الشين، وقرأ الآخرون بضم النون والشين، جمع نشور، مثل صبور وصبر ورسول ورسل، أي: متفرقة وهي الرياح التي تهب من كل ناحية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r4.claim: Between its hands means before the rain.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying wind comes from God’s Spirit with mercy or punishment, so people should not curse it but ask for its good and seek refuge from its evil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p238#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أخذت الناس ريح بطريق مكة وعمر حاج فاشتدت، فقال عمر رضي الله عنه لمن حوله:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r1.claim: The winds carry clouds heavy with rain; the pronoun in ‘we drove it’ refers to the cloud, and a dead land is one needing water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r1.anchor: {حتى إذا أقلت} حملت الرياح {سحابا ثقالا} بالمطر، {سقناه} ورد الكناية إلى السحاب، {لبلد ميت} أي: إلى بلد ميت محتاج إلى الماء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r2.claim: Another explanation takes ‘to a dead land’ as for reviving barren land; ‘by it’ may refer to the cloud or dead land, and the water is rain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه لإحياء بلد ميت لا نبات فيه {فأنزلنا به} أي: بالسحاب. وقيل: بذلك البلد الميت {الماء} يعني: المطر،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r3.claim: Bringing fruits from the land after rain is evidence for bringing the dead back to life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r3.anchor: {فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات كذلك نخرج الموتى} استدل بإحياء الأرض بعد موتها على إحياء الموتى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās say that after the first blast kills everyone, God sends life-water from beneath the Throne; people sprout in their graves, receive spirits, sleep there, then rise at the second blast and say who raised them from their resting place (36:52).
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p239/r4.anchor: قال أبو هريرة وابن عباس: إذا مات الناس كلهم في النفخة الأولى أرسل الله عليهم مطرا كمني الرجال من ماء تحت العرش يدعى ماء الحيوان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r4.claim: These readers use the singular الريح; the remaining readers use the plural الرياح.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي «الريح» على الوحدة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r5.claim: Nushuran is a plural meaning spreading; Ibn ʿĀmir lightens it throughout, while Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use a fatḥa on its nūn as a verbal noun, circumstantial phrase, or absolute object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r5.anchor: جمع نشور بمعنى ناشر، وقرأ ابن عامر «نشرا» بالتخفيف حيث وقع وحمزة والكسائي «نشرا» بفتح النون

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r6.speaker: عاصم
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r6.claim: ʿĀṣim reads bushran as the lightened plural of bashīr, “bringer of good news.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r6.anchor: وعاصم { بشرا } وهو تخفيف بشر جمع بشير وقد قرىء به

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r7.claim: Another reading, bashran, is a verbal noun meaning winds bearing news or announcing good tidings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r7.anchor: و { بشرا } بفتح الباء مصدر بشره بمعنى باشرات، أو للبشارة وبشرى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r8.claim: “Before His mercy” means before rain: the east wind stirs clouds, the north gathers them, the south releases rain, and the west disperses them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r8.anchor: قدام رحمته، يعني المطر فإن الصبا تثير السحاب والشمال تجمعه والجنوب تدره والدبور تفرقه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r9.claim: Aqallat means carried or bore; the derivation invokes the bearer considering the object light.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r9.anchor: أي حملت، واشتقاقه من القلة فإن المقل للشيء يستقله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r10.claim: The clouds are heavy with water; sahāb is a collective plural in the sense of clouds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r10.anchor: بالماء جمعه لأن السحاب جمع بمعنى السحائب

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r11.claim: The pronoun in “We drove it” refers to the cloud, agreeing with its grammatical form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r11.anchor: أي السحاب وإفراد الضمير باعتبار اللفظ

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r12.claim: “To a dead land” can mean for the land, to revive it, or to water it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r13.claim: The pronoun in “by it” can refer to land, cloud, dispatching, or wind, and possibly to water; the preposition is attachment with land at first, locative next, or causal with the other referents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r13.anchor: بالبلد أو بالسحاب أو بالسوق أو بالريح وكذلك. { فأخرجنا به } ويحتمل فيه عود الضمير إلى { الماء } ،

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r14.speaker: author
