BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r14.claim: The fruit phrase covers every kind of fruit.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r15.claim: “Thus We bring out the dead” points either to fruit production or to reviving the dead land; just as God revives it with growth and plants, He raises the dead from graves by restoring souls to assembled bodies with powers and senses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r15.anchor: { كذلك نخرج الموتى } الإشارة فيه إلى إخراج الثمرات، أو إلى إحياء البلد الميت أي كما نحييه بإحداث القوة النامية فيه وتطريتها بأنواع النبات والثمرات،

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r16.claim: The lesson is that whoever can produce this can also resurrect the dead.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:56-57/r16.anchor: فتعلمون أن من قدر على ذلك قدر على هذا

SULAMI:v1p231/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p231/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p231/r1.claim: Some say each wind spreads a kind of mercy: repentance brings love, fear awe, hope intimacy, nearness longing, and longing the fires of anxiety and passionate bewilderment.
SULAMI:v1p231/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : كل ريح تنشر نوعا من الرحمة فريح التوبة تنشر على القلب رحمة المحبة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r5.claim: Rain is one of the greatest forms of mercy, and ongoing cultivation depends on it, on clouds, and on wind; God alone sends the winds.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r5.anchor: وهو من أجل أنواع الرحمة , وهو لا يكون إلا بالسحاب , وهو لا يكون إلا بالريح

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r6.claim: Most readers use the plural “winds,” which Bīqāʿī divides into five types; Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the singular as a generic.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r6.anchor: ووحد ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي على إرادة الجنس

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r7.claim: For the Hijazi and Basran reading, he explains the winds as spread abroad, from nashr, the dispersal of what was folded.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r7.anchor: أي منتشرة جمع نشور من النشر , وهو بسط ما كان مطويا وتفرقه في كل وجه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r8.claim: Wind is not the independent cause of its own spreading, which would make it constant, nor do celestial spheres or stars cause it; their relation to the air is uniform.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r8.anchor: لا لذات الريح وإلا الدام ذلك منها ولا بقوة فلك أو نجم لأن نسبتها إلى الهواء واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r9.claim: “Before His mercy” means before rain; the two hands suggest that wind may bring mercy or punishment, though mercy is more common.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r9.anchor: أي المطر , ولعله عبر فيه باليدين : اليمنى واليسرى

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r10.claim: Winds may gather or disperse clouds, pollinate and cultivate plants, or destroy them, as in autumn; they may heal or kill through heat and cold.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r10.anchor: وتارة تكون مقومة للزروع والأشجار مكملة لها وهي اللواقح , وتارة تكون منمية لها أو مهلكة كما يكون في الخريف

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r11.claim: The winds lift clouds because they are light in relation to them, while the clouds are heavy with water.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r11.anchor: حملتها لقلتها عندها لخفتها عليها { ثقالا } أي بالماء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r12.claim: The plural emphasizes greatness in the winds' sending, while the singular object depicts the cloud's conveyance as one mass whose parts stay together.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r12.anchor: أفرد اللفظ دلالة على غاية العظمة بسوقه مجتمعا كأنه قطعة واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r13.claim: The cloud is driven toward and for the sake of a dead land, one without vegetation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r13.anchor: أي لأجله وإليه { ميت } أي بعد النبات

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r14.claim: The pronoun in “by it” refers either to the land or to the cloud; by water, God brings forth every kind of fruit, including crops in a figurative sense.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r14.anchor: به } أي البلد , أو بسبب ذلك السحاب { الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r15.claim: As God revives barren earth with water and restores a tree's fruit, He can raise bodies from dust and return souls; there is no difference between the two acts of bringing forth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r15.anchor: فهو قادر على إعادة الأشباح وإيداعها الأرواح كما كانت أول مرة , لأنه لا فرق بين الإخرجين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r16.claim: This is a second proof of resurrection after establishing the beginning, given so people may remember God's power to raise the dead.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p44/r16.anchor: دليلا ثانيا في غاية الدلالة على القدرة على البعث

DURR-FULL:v3p477/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r3.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r3.claim: Asim recited the plural الرياح and read بشرا with a light bāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r3.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {وهو الذي يرسل الرياح} على الجماع (بشرا) خفيفة بالباء

DURR-FULL:v3p477/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r4.claim: Al-Suddi describes winds drawing clouds from between the horizons, spreading them across the sky, then rain flowing onto them and falling from them.
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r4.anchor: عن السدي في الآية قال: إن الله يرسل الريح فتأتي بالسحاب من بين الخافقين - طرف السماء والأرض من حيث يلتقيان -

DURR-FULL:v3p477/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r5.claim: The winds as glad tidings before God's mercy means that people rejoice at them.
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {بشرا بين يدي رحمته} قال: يستبشر بها الناس

DURR-FULL:v3p477/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن اليماني
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r6.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Yamani recited بشرا as a form derived from the sense of bearers of glad tidings.
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن اليماني أنه كان يقرأها {بشرا} من قبل مبشرات

DURR-FULL:v3p477/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r7.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies God's mercy in the phrase before it as rain, and compares bringing out the dead to resurrection and plants emerging through water.
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r7.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {بين يدي رحمته} قال: هو المطر وفي قوله {كذلك نخرج الموتى} قال: وكذلك تخرجون

DURR-FULL:v3p477/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r8.claim: Mujahid says God will raise the dead by rain: earth splits, each soul falls to its body, and the dead are revived as the earth is revived.
DURR-FULL:v3p477/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {كذلك نخرج الموتى} قال: إذا أراد الله أن يخرج الموتى تمطر الماء حتى تشقق الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi describes God sending winds that gather clouds from between the horizons, spread them through the sky, open the sky’s gates to rain on them, and then release rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى قوله : وهو الذين يرسل الرياح بشرا قال : ان الله يرسل الرياح فتاتي بالسحاب من بين الخافقين طرف السماء والأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r2.speaker: ابن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Kaʿb, transmitted through a group of Successors, says Quranic forms of “winds” signify mercy; the text then gives both a mercy and a chastisement gloss for the singular form.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r2.anchor: عن جماعة من التابعين ، عن ابن كعب رضى الله عنه قال : كل شيء في القران من الرياح فهي رحمة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the winds are glad tidings because people rejoice at them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس في قوله : وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته قال : فيستبشر بها الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله اليمامي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r4.claim: Abdullah al-Yamami is reported to read the phrase as “bushran min qabli mubashshirat.”
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r4.anchor: كان عبد الله اليمامي ، يقرؤها بشر من قبل مبشرات

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the mercy preceded by the winds is rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r5.anchor: عن السدى قوله : بين يدي رحمته واما رحمته فهو المطر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra says no rain falls except according to a measure.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r6.anchor: ان أبا هريرة رضى الله عنه قال : ما نزل مطر الا بميزان

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r7.claim: Ikrima says God sends water down from the seventh heaven, where a drop lands on a cloud like a camel.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1501#2/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : ينزل الله الماء من السماء السابعة فتقع القطرة منه على السحابة مثل البعير

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r1.speaker: خالد بن يزيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r1.claim: Khalid ibn Yazid says some water comes from the sky and some from clouds fed by the sea; thunder and lightning sweeten the latter, but sea water alone produces no vegetation, which grows from sky water.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r1.anchor: عن سيار ، عن خالد بن يزيد قال : كنا عند عبد الملك بن مروان فذكروا الماء فقال خالد بن يزيد : منه من السماء

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets bringing out the dead as sending rain until the earth splits open over them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : كذلك نخرج الموتى نمطر السماء حتى تشقق عنهم الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says people will likewise be brought out and resurrected as crops emerge when watered.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1502/r3.anchor: عن السدى قوله : كذلك نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون وكذلك تخرجون ، وكذلك النشور كما يخرج الزرع بالماء

AKHFASH:v1p328/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p328/r1.claim: The wind word بشرا is related to النشور as a plural expression; Arabic says ريح نشور and رياح نشر.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r1.anchor: وقال {وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته} لأنها جماعة "النشور" وتقول: "ريح نشور" و"رياح نشر"

AKHFASH:v1p328/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r2.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p328/r2.claim: Some derive the alternative نشرا from the verb نشرها, to spread them.

AKHFASH:v1p328/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p328/r3.claim: Qur'anic syntax can use fronting and postponement; in the opening of this sūra, the warning purpose is tied to the revealed Book despite the intervening phrase فلا يكن في صدرك حرج منه.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r3.anchor: وقال في أول هذه السورة {كتاب أنزل إليك} [2] {لتنذر به} [2] {فلا يكن في صدرك حرج منه} [2] هكذا تأويلها على التقديم والتأخير.

AKHFASH:v1p328/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p328/r4.claim: In the story of Solomon's letter, the sense is to see what they reply and then turn away; the order ثم تول عنهم فانظر is displaced.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r4.anchor: والمعنى - والله أعلم - {فانظر ماذا يرجعون} {ثم تول عنهم}

AKHFASH:v1p328/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p328/r5.claim: In 16:43–44, بالبينات والزبر belongs with the messengers being sent, before the instruction to ask the People of Reminder.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r5.anchor: والمعنى - والله أعلم - {ومآ أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم} {بالبينات والزبر} {فاسألوا أهل الذكر} {إن كنتم لا تعلمون}

AKHFASH:v1p328/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p328/r6.claim: Akhfash reorders the Ghāfir clause so the messengers arrive with proofs and the rejoicing concerns what they possessed; he treats the phrase as an example of displaced order.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r6.anchor: والمعنى - والله أعلم - {فلما جآءتهم رسلهم بالبينات} {من العلم} {فرحوا بما عندهم}

AKHFASH:v1p328/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r7.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p328/r7.claim: Some instead take من العلم as describing knowledge they already possessed; they rejoiced in that knowledge, although it was ignorance.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم {فرحوا بما} هو {عندهم من العلم} أي: كان عندهم العلم وهو جهل

AKHFASH:v1p328/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r8.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p328/r8.claim: An Arabic letter formula أما بعد حفظك الله وعافاك فإني كتبت إليك places words between أما بعد and its intended فإني, illustrating displacement.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r8.anchor: يكتب الرجل: "أما بعد حفظك الله وعافاك فإني كتبت إليك" فقوله "فإني" محمول على "أما بعد"

AKHFASH:v1p328/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r9.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p328/r9.claim: An unidentified kāmil poem is cited as another example of poetic fronting and postponement; the gloss rearranges the words around النساء الجلس.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r9.anchor: خير من القوم العصاة أميرهم * يا قوم فاستحيوا النساء الجلس

AKHFASH:v1p328/r10.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p328/r10.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p328/r10.claim: An unidentified basīṭ poem is also cited as a poetic instance of word-order displacement.
AKHFASH:v1p328/r10.anchor: الشمش طالعة ليست بكاسفة * تبكي عليك نجوم الليل والقمرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r1.claim: The address initially targets polytheists, and the emphatic inna answers their denial that God alone is Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r1.anchor: فالخطاب موجه إلى المشركين ابتداء ، ولذلك كان للتأكيد بحرف ( إن ) موقعه لرد إنكار المشركين انفراد الله بالربوبيه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r2.claim: The address can also include Muslims: these statements deepen their knowledge of God, and inna marks an important message relevant to both groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p159#2/r2.anchor: وإذ كان ما اشتملت عليه هذه الآية يزيد المسلمين بصيرة بعظم مجد الله وسعة ملكه ، ويزيدهم ذكرى بدلائل قدرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r1.claim: The winds clause coordinates with the night-and-day clause, or with the statement that creation and command belong to God; its link follows the mention of mercy in 7:56.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r1.anchor: جملة : { وهو الذي يرسل الرياح } عطف على جملة : { يغشي الليل النهار } ( الأعراف : 54 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r2.claim: Sending winds is the primary point because it demonstrates God’s power and governance; the rain also embeds a reminder of His general mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r2.anchor: فذكر إرسال الرياح هو المقصود الأهم لأنه دليل على عظم القدرة والتدبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r3.claim: The weather sequence is not an attempt to teach meteorology and does not claim that winds are sent only before rain or that rain follows only winds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r3.anchor: وذلك لا يقتضي أن الرياح لا ترسل إلا للتبشير بالمطر ، ولا أن المطر لا ينزل إلا عقب إرسال الرياح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r4.claim: The passage alludes to abundant rain promised to believers and drought and hunger warned for polytheists, as in 72:16 and 44:10.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r4.anchor: وفيه تعريض ببشارة المؤمنين بإغداق الغيث عليهم ونذارة المشركين بالقحط والجوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r5.claim: Sending is a metaphor for winds moving from where they blow to a destination; personifying them as dispatched messengers suits their subjection to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r5.anchor: وأطلق الإرسال على الانتقال على وجه الاستعارة ، فإرسال الرياح هبوبها من المكان الذي تهب فيه ووصولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r6.claim: Because wind remains within the air sphere, its movement from place to place resembles dispatch more than creation; he refers to 2:164.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r6.anchor: ومن بدائع هذه الاستعارة أن الريح لا تفارق كرة الهواء كما تقدم عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r7.claim: Riyāḥ is the plural of rīḥ, a usage previously discussed in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p178#2/r7.anchor: والرياح : جمع ريح ، وقد تقدم في سورة البقرة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.claim: Bayna yaday originally means in front of someone, close by; its conventional sense is ‘in front,’ contrasted with what is behind at 2:255.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r1.anchor: وأصل معنى قولهم : بين يدي فلان ، أنه يكون أمامه بقرب منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.claim: The expression extends figuratively to something that precedes another soon, even without literal hands or spatial front; here the winds precede rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r2.anchor: وساغ أن تستعمل مجازا في التقدم والسبق القريب ، كقوله تعالى : { إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.claim: Here ‘mercy’ means rain by naming the source for its product, as the context shows; Arabic usage does not establish mercy as a name for rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r3.anchor: والرحمة هذه أريد بها المطر ، فهو من إطلاق المصدر على المفعول ، لأن الله يرحم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.claim: The main purpose is to rebuke polytheists and refute their association of partners, with reminding and reflection for believers following secondarily.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r4.anchor: والمقصد الأول من قوله : { وهو الذي يرسل الرياح } تقريع المشركين وتفنيد إشراكهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.claim: The relative clause presents the winds’ and rain’s true agent as something its addressees know, though polytheists ignore or feign ignorance of that identity and use passive or star-based descriptions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r5.anchor: لأن المشركين يعلمون أن للرياح مصرفا وأن للمطر منزلا ، غير أنهم يذهلون أو يتذاهلون عن تعيين ذلك الفاعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.claim: The clause identifies God as the agent, answering an implicit request to identify the sender; it is not restrictive predication since polytheists did not claim another sends the winds, and resembles 2:16.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p180#2/r6.anchor: فهو بمنزلة الجواب عن استفهام مقصود منه طلب التعيين في نحو قولهم : أراحل أنت أم ثاو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r1.claim: The initial hatta sets the endpoint of the winds’ advance before mercy: they spread clouds, carry them, drive them to a land, and rain falls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r1.anchor: و { حتى } ابتدائية وهي غاية لمضمون قوله : { بشرا بين يدي رحمته }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r2.claim: The successive clauses form several stages of the endpoint, beginning with the winds lifting clouds, then their heaviness and movement, and finally rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r2.anchor: وكانت الغاية مجزأة أجزاء فأولها مضمون قوله : { أقلت } أي الرياح السحاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r3.claim: Thiqāl describes clouds slow to move because they hold moist vapor and are expected to bring rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r3.anchor: الثقال : البطيئة التنقل لما فيها من رطوبة الماء ، وهو البخار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r4.speaker: أبو الطيب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Ṭayyib’s verse contrasts a beneficial slow grant with fast barren clouds, supporting the description of rain clouds as slow-moving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r4.anchor:
ومن أحسن معاني أبي الطيب قوله في : ( حسن الاعتذار ) :
ومن الخير بطء سيبك عني
أسرع السحب في المسير الجهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r5.claim: Winds stir vapor on the earth and gather further moisture from seas, rivers, lakes, and damp lands; this process is also described at 30:48.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r5.anchor: وذلك أن الرياح تحرك الأبخرة التي على سطح الأرض ، وتمدها برطوبات تسوقها إليها من الجهات الندية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r6.claim: Aqallat means ‘carried’: it derives from qilla because a carrier counts its load as little, and the hamza is causative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى { أقلت } ، حملت مشتق من القلة لأن الحامل يعد محموله قليلا فالهمزة فيه للجعل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r7.claim: The winds raise vapor to a cold level where it condenses into cloud; clouds join, grow heavy, liquefy, and fall as rain, unlike the initial stirring described in 30:48.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p181#2/r7.anchor: فهنالك ينقبض البخار وتتجمع أجزاؤه فيصير سحابات ، وكلما انضمت سحابة إلى أخرى حصلت منهما سحابة أثقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r1.claim: Saḥāb is a collective noun that permits masculine agreement by form and collective agreement by sense; the verse uses plural ثقالا and singular سقناه.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r1.anchor: والسحاب اسم جمع لسحابة فلذلك جاز اجراؤه على اعتبار التذكير نظرا لتجرد لفظه عن علامة التأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r2.claim: The Prophet’s expression ‘I saw cows being slaughtered’ exemplifies agreement according to a collective plural sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r2.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم و ( رأيت بقرا تذبح )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r3.claim: Saq means driving something that walks by following and urging it; here it metaphorically describes cloud moved by God’s causes, or pictures wind driving cloud like a handler driving a mount.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r3.anchor: وحقيقة السوق أنه تسيير ما يمشي ومسيره وراءه يزجيه ويحثه ، وهو هنا مستعار لتسير السحاب بأسبابه التي جعلها الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r4.claim: The lām in ‘for a land’ marks purpose and signals divine care for that land, which explains the wording instead of ‘to.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r4.anchor: واللام في قوله : { لبلد } لام العلة ، أي لأجل بلد ميت ، وفي هذه اللام دلالة على العناية الربانية بذلك البلد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r5.claim: Balad means a broad expanse of land.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r6.claim: ‘Dead’ describes a land without vegetation; calling the land dead is itself a figurative attribution because its plants and fruit are what die.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r6.anchor: والميت : مجاز أطلق على الجانب الذي انعدم منه النبات ، وإسناد الموت المجازي إلى البلد هو أيضا مجاز عقلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r7.claim: The bāʾ in ‘We brought forth by it’ may refer to the land, making bāʾ mean ‘in,’ or to water as the instrument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r7.anchor: والضمير المجرور بالباء في قوله : فأخرجنا به يجوز أن يعود إلى البلد ، فيكون الباء بمعنى ( في )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r8.claim: ‘All fruits’ is genuinely exhaustive across all dead lands; for one particular land it means all locally familiar fruits, with min partitive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p182/r8.anchor: والاستغراق في { كل الثمرات } استغراق حقيقي ، لأن البلد الميت ليس معينا بل يشمل كل بلد ميت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r1.claim: The resurrection clause is a parenthetical exhortation and proof; ‘likewise’ points to bringing fruit from dead land, whose revival after death approximates resurrection, though its actual mode is beyond human understanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r1.anchor: وجملة : { كذلك نخرج الموتى } معترضة استطرادا للموعظة والاستدلال على تقريب البعث الذي يستبعدونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r2.claim: ‘So that you may remember’ resumes the discussion: believers gain reflection and faith, while polytheism and denial of resurrection should fall away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r2.anchor: والرجاء ناشىء عن الجمل المتقدمة من قوله : { وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r3.claim: The majority read tadhakkarūna with a doubled dhāl, assimilating the second tāʾ after turning it into dhāl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تذكرون } بتشديد الذال على إدغام التاء الثانية في الذال بعد قلبها ذالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r4.speaker: عاصم في رواية حفص
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r4.claim: In Ḥafṣ’s transmission, ʿĀṣim reads tadhakkarūna with a light dhāl by deleting one of the two tāʾs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p183#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية حفص { تذكرون } بتخفيف الذال على حذف إحدى التاءين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya presents the rain-and-fruit passage as a sign inviting reflection and inference.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r1.anchor: هذه آية اعتبار واستدلال، وقرأ نافع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r2.claim: They read الرياح in the plural and نشرا with both nun and shin vocalized; Abu Hatim also reports this form from al-Hasan, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, and Abu Rajaʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r2.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو «الرياح» بالجمع «نشرا» بضم النون والشين، قال أبو حاتم: وهي قراءة الحسن وأبي عبد الرحمن وأبي رجاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r3.claim: He reads الريح in the singular and نشرا with both nun and shin vocalized.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «الريح» واحدة «نشرا» بضمها أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r4.claim: He reads الرياح in the plural and نشرا with a vocalized nun and quiescent shin; Abu Hatim reports this from several other readers too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر «الرياح» جمعا «نشرا» بضم النون وسكون الشين، قال أبو حاتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r5.claim: They read الريح in the singular and نشرا with fatḥa on the nun and a quiescent shin; Abu Hatim names Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Zirr, and others for this reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي، «الريح» واحدة، «نشرا» بفتح النون وسكون الشين، قال أبو حاتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r6.speaker: ابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r6.claim: He transmits Masruq’s reading نشرا with fatḥa on both nun and shin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن جني قراءة مسروق «نشرا» بفتح النون والشين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r7.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r7.claim: He reads الرياح in the plural with بشرا, baʾ vocalized and shin quiescent; another narration from him vocalizes both letters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم «الرياح» جماعة «بشرا» بالباء المضمومة والشين الساكنة، وروي عنه «بشرا» بضم الباء والشين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والسلمي وابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r8.claim: They read بشرا with baʾ and shin both vocalized, the same variant also transmitted from ʿAsim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r8.anchor: وروي عنه «بشرا» بضم الباء والشين، وقرأ بها ابن عباس والسلمي وابن أبي عبلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r9.speaker: محمد بن السميفع وأبو قطيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r9.claim: They read بشرى on the fuʿla pattern with a vocalized baʾ; this is also transmitted from Abu Yahya and Abu Nufayl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميفع وأبو قطيب «بشرى» على وزن فعلى بضم الباء، ورويت عن أبي يحيى وأبي نوفل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r10.claim: He reads بشرا with fatḥa on baʾ and a quiescent shin; al-Zahrawi says this reading is also transmitted from ʿAsim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي «بشرا» بفتح الباء وسكون الشين، قال الزهراوي: ورويت هذه عن عاصم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r11.claim: Plural الرياح is more apt because Qurʾanic plural winds accompany mercy, whereas singular الريح is usually associated with punishment; Ibn ʿAṭiyya links this reasoning to Yahya ibn Yaʿmar, Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ, and ʿAsim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r11.anchor: ومن جمع الريح في هذه الآية فهو أسعد، وذلك أن الرياح حيث وقعت في القرآن فهي مقترنة بالرحمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r12.claim: When the wind blew, the Prophet prayed that it be beneficial winds and not a destructive wind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p411#2/r12.anchor: وفي الحديث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا هبت الريح يقول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r1.claim: Rain-bearing winds are dispersed and gentle, arriving from different directions; their separated parts and slightly varying courses suit the plural form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r1.anchor: والمعنى في هذا كله بين، وذلك أن ريح السقيا والمطر أنها هي منتشرة لينة تجيء من هاهنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r2.claim: Punitive winds are a single connected, violent force, so the singular is apt for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r2.anchor: وتوصف بالكثرة ريح الصر والعذاب، عاصفة صرصر جسد واحد شديدة المر مهلكة بقوتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r3.claim: The wind in the ship passage is singular because the ships move under one continuous current; it is called good to distinguish it from a harmful wind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r3.anchor: وكذلك أفردت الريح في قوله تعالى: وجرين بهم بريح طيبة [يونس: 22] من حيث جري السفن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r4.claim: Solomon’s wind is singular because it moved continuously at his command or swept through his fields as one connected force.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r4.anchor: وكذلك ريح سليمان عليه السلام إنما كانت تجري بأمره أو تعصف في حقوله وهي متصلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r5.claim: A singular reading here can still mean wind as a generic class, and the qualification by نشر removes ambiguity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r5.anchor: فمن قرأ في هذه الآية الريح بالإفراد فإنما يريد به اسم الجنس، وأيضا فتقييدها ب «نشر» يزيل الاشتراك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r6.claim: إرسال the wind means setting it in motion, releasing it, or letting it flow.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r6.anchor: والإرسال في الريح هو بمعنى والإجراء والإطلاق والإسالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r7.claim: The small plural of ريح is أرواح and the large plural is رياح; the root wāw becomes yaʾ under the preceding kasra in the singular and large plural, while the small plural remains sound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r7.anchor: والريح تجمع في القليل أرواح وفي الكثير رياح لأن العين من الريح واو انقلبت في الواحد ياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r8.claim: With both nun and shin vocalized, نشرا may be an attributive plural of ناشر, meaning winds that spread something folded or bring life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r8.anchor: وأما «نشرا» بضم النون والشين فيحتمل أن يكون جمع ناشر على النسب أي ذات نشر من الطي أو نشور من الحياة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r9.claim: The same vocalization may instead be the plural of نشور, on the patterns رسول/رسل, صبور/صبر, and شكور/شكر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r9.anchor: ويحتمل «نشرا» أن يكون جمع نشور بفتح النون وضم الشين كرسول ورسل وصبور وصبر وشكور وشكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r10.claim: Another analysis takes نشرا as passive in sense, like مركوب expressed by ركوب.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r10.anchor: ويحتمل «نشرا» أن يكون كالمفعول بمعنى منشور كركوب بمعنى مركوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r11.claim: It may also be an active-participle form because the winds spread the clouds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من أبنية اسم الفاعل لأنها تنشر الحساب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r12.speaker: شاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r12.claim: The forms شاهد/شهد and نازل/نزل illustrate the pattern used in the grammatical analysis of نشرا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r12.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: أو تنزلون فإنا معشر نزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r13.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r13.claim: His line إنا لمثلكم يا قومنا قتل is cited as another witness to the pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r13.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: [البسيط] إنا لمثلكم يا قومنا قتل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r14.claim: The reading with a quiescent shin after vocalized nun lightens the doubled shin of نشرا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r14.anchor: وأما من قرأ «نشرا» بضم النون وسكون الشين فإنما خفف الشين من قوله نشرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r15.claim: With fatḥa on nun and a quiescent shin, نشرا is a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial adverb from الريح.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r15.anchor: وأما من قرأ «نشرا» بفتح النون وسكون الشين فهو مصدر في موضع الحال من الريح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r16.claim: That verbal noun may mean spreading rather than folding, or may refer to revival.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r16.anchor: ويحتمل في المعنى أن يراد به من النشر الذي هو خلاف الطي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r17.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r17.claim: The line about the dead person who spreads to life supports the revival sense of نشر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r17.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: [السريع] يا عجبا للميت الناشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r18.speaker: ابن الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r18.claim: The rare reading with both nun and shin open is an attributive noun meaning winds possessing نشر, or spreading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r18.anchor: وأما من قرأ «نشرا» بفتح النون والشين وهي قراءة شاذة فهو اسم وهو على النسب، قال أبو الفتح أي ذوات نشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r19.speaker: ابن الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r19.claim: He explains نشر as livestock spreading out at night to graze, a comparison for clouds spreading widely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r19.anchor: والنشر أن تنتشر الغنم بالليل فترعى، فشبه السحاب، في انتشاره وعمومه بذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r20.claim: With baʾ and shin vocalized, بشرا is the plural of بشير, like نذير/نذر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r20.anchor: وأما «بشرا» بضم الباء والشين فجمع بشير كنذير ونذر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r21.claim: The form with quiescent shin is a shortened pronunciation of the same plural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r22.claim: With fatḥa on baʾ and quiescent shin, بشرا is a verbal noun; بشرى is also a verbal noun, each used circumstantially.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r22.anchor: و «بشرا» بفتح الباء وسكون الشين مصدر و «بشرى» مصدر أيضا في موضع الحال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r23.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r23.claim: Here الرحمة means rain, and بين يدي means before it; the phrase is metaphorical here but literal for objects before a person’s hands.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p412/r23.anchor: و «الرحمة» في هذه الآية المطر، وبين يدي أي أمام رحمته وقدامها وهي هنا استعارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r1.claim: أقلت means the wind lifted the cloud from the ground and carried it aloft; the root also suggests that a lifter regards what is raised as little once it is within his power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r1.anchor: وأقلت معناه: رفعت من الأرض واستقلت بها، ومنه القلة وكأن المقل يرد ما رفع قليلا إذا قدر عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r2.claim: ثقالا means laden with water; Arabs describe clouds as heavy and dalūḥ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r2.anchor: وثقالا معناه من الماء، والعرب تصف السحاب بالثقل والدلح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r3.speaker: قيس بن الخطيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r3.claim: His verse supplies an example of describing a cloud as dalūḥ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r3.anchor: ومنه قول قيس بن الخطيم: [المتقارب] بأحسن منها ولا مزنة ... دلوح تكشف أدجانها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r4.claim: The wind literally drives the cloud from behind; the pronoun in سقناه refers to the cloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r4.anchor: والريح تسوق السحاب من ورائها فهو سوق حقيقة، والضمير في سقناه عائد على السحاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r5.claim: The action is grammatically attached to God’s pronoun because it is an act of beneficence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r5.anchor: واستند الفعل إلى ضمير اسم الله تعالى من حيث هو إنعام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r6.claim: Calling the land dead is metaphorical, because it is broad, barren, and its plants have withered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r6.anchor: وصفة البلد بالموت استعارة بسبب سعته وجدوبته وتصويح نباته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r7.claim: They read ميت with an ungeminated, quiescent yaʾ; the remaining readers geminate it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم والأعمش: «لبلد ميت» بسكون الياء وشدها الباقون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r8.claim: In فأنزلنا به, the pronoun may refer to cloud, land, or water, with water the most apparent antecedent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r8.anchor: والضمير في قوله: فأنزلنا به يحتمل أن يعود على الحساب أي منه، ويحتمل أن يعود على البلد، ويحتمل أن يعود على الماء وهو أظهرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r9.claim: He describes winds bringing clouds from the meeting horizons, spreading them across the sky, then rain descending onto them and falling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r9.anchor: وقال السدي في تفسير هذه الآية: إن الله تعالى يرسل الرياح فتأتي بالسحاب من بين الخافقين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this detailed sequence is not established from the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r10.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا التفصيل لم يثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r11.claim: One reading of كذلك نخرج الموتى is an analogy: the power that brings water and fruit from barren land is also power to raise the dead from their graves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r11.anchor: أحدهما أن يراد كهذه القدرة العظيمة في إنزال الماء وإخراج الثمرات به من الأرض المجدبة هي القدرة على إحياء الموتى من الأجداث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r12.claim: Alternatively, it predicts that rain will fall on the dead and revive them, making the words a literal report rather than a comparison.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد أن هكذا يصنع بالأموات من نزول المطر عليهم حتى يحيوا به فيكون الكلام خبرا لا مثلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r13.claim: A report cited by al-Tabari says rain from beneath the Throne, called the water of life, falls for forty years after the first blast; bodies grow like crops, receive souls, sleep, then rise after the second blast and hear the caller identify the promised resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p413/r13.anchor: الحديث الذي ذكره الطبري عن أبي هريرة أن الناس إذا ماتوا في النفخة الأولى مطر عليهم مطر من ماء تحت العرش

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r1.claim: Bushran is as if the winds give good news; God's mercy here is rain, called mercy because it comes through His mercy.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r1.anchor: كأنها تبشر. ورحمته ها هنا: المطر، سماه رحمة: لأنه كان برحمته.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r2.claim: On the reading nushuran, the word means either plural nushūr or something scattered; the idiom asks God to gather one's scattered affairs.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r2.anchor: ومن قرأها (نشرا بين يدي رحمته) أراد جمع نشور ونشر الشيء ما تفرق منه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r3.claim: Aqallat means the clouds carried or bore water; istiqlāl is used for what one carries.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p169#2/r3.anchor: أي حملت. ومنه يقال: ما أستقل به.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r1.claim: These reciters read الرياح in the plural; Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Kisai read the singular الريح, which can also denote many winds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم الرياح على الجمع وقرأ ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي الريح على التوحيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير ونافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r2.claim: These reciters read نشرا with ḍamma on both nūn and shīn, as a plural of نشور for a pleasant wind blowing from every direction; Abu Ubayda glosses it as dispersed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير ونافع نشرا بضم النون والشين أرادوا جمع نشور وهي الريح الطيبة الهبوب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r3.claim: For the wind's description, أبو علي allows نشور to mean revived, spreading, or spreading life; al-Fuqasi's verse makes أنشر الله الريح mean God revived the wind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r3.anchor: والدليل على أن إنشار الربح إحياؤها قول الفقعسي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r4.speaker: الفقعسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r4.claim: Al-Fuqasi's line about the south wind reviving a breeze and its waters supports interpreting نشر wind as life or revival.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r4.anchor: وهبت له ريح الجنوب وأحييت له ريدة يحيي المياه نسيمها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r5.speaker: شاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r5.claim: A cited poem describes the wind dying, supporting the usage of wind as something that can be alive or dead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p216#2/r5.anchor: إني لأرجو أن تموت الريح فأقعد اليوم وأستريح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r1.speaker: ابن القاسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r1.claim: The reading نشرا can be analyzed as a plural of نشور, like عمود/عمد, or as a plural of ناشر, like غائب/غيب.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون جمعا للنشور كما قالوا عمود وعمد وإهاب وأهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r2.speaker: القراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r2.claim: All reciters use nūn in the word in this reading set; other reciters use bāʾ instead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r2.anchor: وكل القراء نون الكلمة وكذلك اختلافهم في الفرقان والنمل هذه قراءات من قرأ بالنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r3.speaker: عاصم إلا المفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r3.claim: Asim, except al-Mufaddal, reads بشرى with bāʾ and a silent shīn; al-Anbari analyzes it as a plural of بشيرة, one that announces rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r3.anchor: فقرأ عاصم إلا المفضل بشرى بالباء المضمومة وسكون الشين مثل فعلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r4.speaker: ابن خثيم وابن جذلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r4.claim: Ibn Khuthaym and Ibn Jadhlem have the same ب reading but add nunation to the final ra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن خثيم وابن جذلم مثله إلا أنهما نونا الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r5.speaker: أبو الجوزاء وأبو عمران وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r5.claim: These reciters read the bāʾ and shīn with ḍamma, treating the form as a plural of بشيرة.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء وأبو عمران وابن أبي عبلة بضم الباء والشين وهذا على أنها جمع بشيرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r6.claim: Here mercy means rain, named mercy because it comes as a mercy; أقلت means carried.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r6.anchor: والرحمة هاهنا المطر سماه رحمة لأنه كان بالرحمة وأقلت بمعنى حملت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r7.claim: The singular form of السحاب denotes a collective mass of clouds.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r8.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r8.claim: The cloud is named السحاب for its movement through the air.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p218/r8.anchor: قال ابن فارس سمي السحاب لانسحابه في الهواء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r1.claim: ثقالا means heavy with water; سقناه refers back to السحاب, grammatically singular.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ثقالا ﴾ أي الماء وقوله تعالى ﴿ سقناه ﴾ رد الكناية إلى لفظ السحاب ولفظه لفظ واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r2.claim: لبلد may mean “to a land” or “for reviving a land”; dead land is land that does not grow and needs rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r2.anchor: وفي قوله لبلد قولان أحدهما إلى بلد والثاني لإحياء بلد والميت الذي لا ينبت فيه فهو محتاج إلى المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r3.claim: For فأنزلنا به, the pronoun may refer to the cloud or the rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r3.anchor: وفي قوله ﴿ فأنزلنا به ﴾ ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أن الكناية ترجع إلى السحاب والثاني إلى المطر ذكرهما الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r4.claim: For فأنزلنا به, another possible antecedent is the land; the following pronoun in فأخرجنا به could likewise refer to cloud, rain, or land.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r4.anchor: والثالث إلى البلد ذكره ابن الأنباري فأما هاء ﴿ فأخرجنا به ﴾ فتحتمل الأقوال الثلاثة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r5.claim: Raising the dead resembles reviving the dead land.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ كذلك نخرج الموتى ﴾ أي كما أحيينا هذا البلد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r6.claim: Mujahid says God revives the dead through rain, as He revived the dead land through it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد نحيي الموتى بالمطر كما أحيينا البلد الميت به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says rain like men's semen falls between the two trumpet blasts, and people grow in their graves as they grew in their mothers' wombs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس يرسل الله تعالى بين النفختين مطرا كمني الرجال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219#2/r1.claim: لعل expresses expectation; people are addressed in terms of the hope one person has of another, meaning the signs should prompt inference of God's oneness and resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p219#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج لعل ترج وإنما خوطب العباد على ما يرجوه بعضهم من بعض

MAJAZ:v1p217/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p217/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p217/r2.claim: Aqallat saḥāban means the winds drove or carried a cloud.

MAJAZ:v1p217/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p217/r3.claim: Nakd means scanty and difficult in harsh conditions.
MAJAZ:v1p217/r3.anchor: «لا يخرج إلا نكدا» (57) أي قليلا عسرا فى شدة قال:

MAJAZ:v1p217/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p217/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p217/r4.claim: An unnamed poet uses nakd for a small, poor gift.
MAJAZ:v1p217/r4.anchor: لا تنجز الوعد إن وعدت وإن ... أعطيت أعطيت تافها نكدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r1.claim: After establishing God's creation and rule and directing people to pray to Him, the passage points to Him as provider and raiser of the dead.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r1.anchor: نبه تعالى على أنه الرزاق، وأنه يعيد الموتى يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r2.claim: The winds spread before the rain-bearing clouds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r2.anchor: أي: ناشرة بين يدي السحاب الحامل للمطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r3.speaker: قراء غير مسمين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r3.claim: Some read the word as بشرا, understood alongside the description of winds as bearers of good tidings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r3.anchor: ومنهم من قرأ {بشرا} كقوله {ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r4.claim: ‘Before His mercy’ means before the rain, supported by verses describing rainfall and the revival of dead earth as God's mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r4.anchor: وقوله: {بين يدي رحمته} أي: بين يدي المطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r5.claim: The winds lift clouds heavy with abundant water; they become weighty, low to the earth, and dark.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r5.anchor: أي: من كثرة ما فيها من الماء، تكون ثقيلة قريبة من الأرض مدلهمة، كما قال زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، رحمه الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r6.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r6.claim: A poem depicts clouds carrying sweet, pure water and the earth carrying heavy rocks, illustrating the imagery of weighty clouds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430/r6.anchor: قال زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، رحمه الله. وأسلمت وجهي لمن أسلمت … له المزن تحمل عذبا زلالا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r1.claim: A dead land is barren and has no vegetation, as another verse describes the dead earth being revived.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r1.anchor: أرض ميتة، مجدبة (4) لا نبات فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r2.claim: Reviving barren earth illustrates bodily resurrection: rain will fall for forty days and bodies will grow in their graves like seed in soil; this is a recurring Qur'anic analogy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p430#2/r2.anchor: ينزل الله، سبحانه وتعالى، ماء من السماء، فتمطر الأرض أربعين يوما، فتنبت منه الأجساد في قبورها كما ينبت الحب في الأرض

NAHHAS:v2p132/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p132/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq calls the poetic use of masculine قريب with a feminine antecedent wrong because masculine and feminine should each agree with their verbs.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هذا خطأ لأن سبيل المذكر والمؤنث أن يجريا على أفعالهما

NAHHAS:v2p132/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v2p132/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains masculine قريب by taking the referent as the masculine word المكان.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r2.anchor: ومذهب أبي عبيدة أن تذكير قريب على تذكير المكان

NAHHAS:v2p132/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r3.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v2p132/r3.claim: ʿAlī b. Sulaymān rejects that explanation: if a place were intended, قريب would be accusative, as in إن زيدا قريبا منك.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r3.anchor: قال علي بن سليمان هذا خطأ ولو كان كما قال لكان قريب منصوبا في القرآن

NAHHAS:v2p132/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r4.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v2p132/r4.claim: Sībawayh permits Abū ʿUbayda's analysis, though rarely, as illustrated by a poem where كلا الفرجين is followed by masculine أنه.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r4.anchor: قد أجاز سيبويه مثله على بعد كما قال

NAHHAS:v2p132/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r5.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p132/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash allows a feminine noun to be treated as masculine, citing an anonymous poem with الأرض and masculine أبقل.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r5.anchor: وقال الأخفش يجوز أن يذكر كما يذكر بعض المؤنث

NAHHAS:v2p132/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p132/r6.claim: A further explanation takes رحمة here to mean rain.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r6.anchor: قال ويجوز أن تكون الرحمة ههنا للمطر

NAHHAS:v2p132/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p132/r7.claim: A sixth explanation treats the masculine form as an adjectival relation, like امرأة طالق or حائض.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r7.anchor: والقول السادس أن يكون هذا على النسب كما يقال امرأة طالق وحائض

NAHHAS:v2p132/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p132/r8.claim: الرياح is the usual plural of ريح; أرواح is the rarer plural because the original wāw shifted to yāʾ after a preceding kasra while quiescent.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r8.anchor: والرياح جمع ريح في أكثر العدد وفي أقله أرواح لأن الياء في ريح منقلبة من واو

NAHHAS:v2p132/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r9.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v2p132/r9.claim: The Two Sanctuaries' readers and Abū ʿAmr read نشرا with damma on both nūn and shīn.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r9.anchor: قرأ أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو ( نشرا ) بضم النون والشين

NAHHAS:v2p132/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
NAHHAS:v2p132/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read نشرا with damma on nūn and a vowelless shīn.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة ( نشرا ) بضم النون وإسكان الشين

NAHHAS:v2p132/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r11.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p132/r11.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read نشرا with fatḥa on nūn and a vowelless shīn.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r11.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي ( نشرا ) بفتح النون وإسكان الشين

NAHHAS:v2p132/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r12.speaker: عاصم
NAHHAS:v2p132/r12.claim: ʿĀṣim reads بشرا with bāʾ and a vowelless shīn; a second narration from him has fatḥa on bāʾ.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r12.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ( بشرا ) بالباء وإسكان الشين والتنوين وروي عنه ( بشرا ) بفتح الباء

NAHHAS:v2p132/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r13.speaker: محمد اليماني
NAHHAS:v2p132/r13.claim: Muḥammad al-Yamānī reads بشرى on the pattern ḥublā.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r13.anchor: وقرأ محمد اليماني ( بشرى بين يدي رحمته ) في وزن حبلى

NAHHAS:v2p132/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p132/r14.claim: A seventh permissible reading is بشرا with damma on bāʾ and shīn; the readings are circumstantial accusatives, and verbal nouns work like قتله صبرا.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r14.anchor: والقراءة السابعة ( بشرا ) بضم الباء والشين قال أبو جعفر وقد ذكرنا معانيها في كتابنا المعاني

NAHHAS:v2p132/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p132/r15.claim: سحاب can be masculine or feminine, and it can take either masculine or feminine singular adjectives.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r15.anchor: ( حتى إذا أقلت سحابا ) يذكر ويؤنث وكذا كل جمع بينه وبين واحدته هاء

NAHHAS:v2p132/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p132/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p132/r16.claim: سقناه لبلد and سقناه إلى بلد mean the same thing.
NAHHAS:v2p132/r16.anchor: ( سقناه لبلد ميت ) وإلى بلد بمعنى واحد

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r4.claim: These readers have plural al-riyāḥ and nushuran, with nushur as a plural like ṣubūr/ṣabr and shukūr/shukr.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: الرياح على الجمع نشرا بضم النون والشين وهو جمع نشور كصبور، وصبر وشكور وشكر.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r5.claim: They read singular al-rīḥ with nashran, meaning a pleasant breeze; Ibn Masʿud and Ibn Abbas are also reported to read it.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي الريح على الواحد نشرا بفتح النون وسكون الشين، والنشر: الريح الطيبة، وهي قراءة ابن مسعود وابن عباس،

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد وخلف
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r6.claim: They choose the singular-wind reading, supported by 77:3.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r6.anchor: واختاره أبو عبيد وخلف، لقوله: (والناشرات نشرا).

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r7.claim: He reads plural al-riyāḥ with nushran, a verbal noun like al-ʿaṣf; the same reading is attributed to al-Hasan and al-Sulami.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر الرياح جمع نشرا بضم النون وسكون الشين، وهو مصدر كالعصف، وهو قراءة الحسن والسلمي.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r8.speaker: عاصم
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r8.claim: He reads plural al-riyāḥ with bushran, from glad tidings, since the winds announce rain; 30:46 supports this sense.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r8.anchor: وقرأ عاصم الرياح جمع بشرا بالباء وضمها وسكون الشين من البشارة يعني أنها تبشر بالمطر، يدل عليه قوله: (الرياح مبشرات)

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r9.speaker: مسروق
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r9.claim: Masruq is reported to read nushuran with both initial vowels open, meaning manshūr, spread out.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r9.anchor: وروي عن مسروق نشرا بفتحتين؛ أراد منشورا.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r10.claim: Nashr is the opposite of folding; wind is likened to folded cloth because it is unseen, then becomes perceptible like cloth being unfolded.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r10.anchor: النشر: خلاف الطي، والريح بمنزلة المطوي في أنه لا يدرك، ثم صار يدرك، فكان كنشر الثوب،

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r11.claim: Bushr, with bāʾ, derives from glad tidings, as does bashīr.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r11.anchor: والبشر بالباء: من البشارة، ومنه البشير.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r12.claim: Iq lāl means carrying something; istaqalla with its load means it rose up bearing it.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r12.anchor: والإقلال: حمل الشيء، يقال: استقل بحمله استقلالا: إذا نهض به، وأقله يقله إقلالا: إذا حمله.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r13.claim: Cloud is the moving mass in the sky, and heaviness is the lower part bearing down.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r13.anchor: والسحاب: الغيم الجاري في السماء، واحدها سحابة، وهو من الإسحاب سحبه سحبا والثقل: اعتماد السفلى.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r14.claim: Driving a thing means urging it onward until it moves quickly.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r14.anchor: والسوق: حثه الشيء في السير حتى يقع الإسراع، ساقه يسوقه سوقا.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r15.claim: One analysis gives the lām in li-balad the sense of ilā; the cited lām in 99:5 and 7:43 likewise means ilā.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r15.anchor: قيل: اللام في قوله: لبلد بمعنى (إلى)، وحروف الصفات تتبادل، قال تعالى: (بأن ربك أوحى لها) أي: إليها، و(هدانا لهذا) أي إلى هذا.

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r16.claim: Another analysis makes the lām purposive: God made the cloud and drove it to revive a dead land.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r16.anchor: وقيل هو بمعنى الإضافة أي: أنشأ السحاب، وسقناه لإحياء بلد ميت،

JISHUMI:v4p2594/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r17.claim: The pronoun in saqunāhu refers back to the cloud.
JISHUMI:v4p2594/r17.anchor: والكناية في قوله: سقناه ترجع إلى السحاب.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r8.claim: The reading nushuran is a verbal noun of nashara; its accusative is either cognate with sending/spreading or circumstantial, meaning spread out.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r8.anchor: قرىء : ( نشرا وهو مصدر نشر . وانتصابه إما لأن أرسل ونشر متقاربان ، فكأنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r9.claim: Nushuran is also read as the plural of nushūr.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r9.anchor: ونشرا جمع نشور . ونشرا تخفيف نشر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r10.claim: Nashran is a lightened form of nashr, like rusul and rusl.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r11.speaker: مسروق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r11.claim: Masrūq reads nushuran to mean things spread out, with faʿl used in a passive sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ مسروق : ( نشرا ) ، بمعنى منشورات ، فعل بمعنى مفعول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r12.claim: Bushran is the plural of bashīr.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r13.anchor: وبشرا جمع بشير . وبشرا بتخفيفه . وبشرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r14.claim: Bushran with fatḥa is a verbal noun from bashshara, meaning bearers of glad tidings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r14.anchor: وبشرا بفتح الباء مصدر من بشره بمعنى بشره ، أي باشرات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r15.claim: The winds come before God's mercy, meaning the rain, among the greatest blessings and most beneficial effects.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r15.anchor: بين يدى رحمته } أمام رحمته ، وهي الغيث الذي هو من أتم النعم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r16.claim: Aqallat means that the wind-borne clouds carried and lifted their load; the word derives from the lifter's sense that the load is small.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r16.anchor: أقلت } حملت ورفعت ، واشتقاق الإقلال من القلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r17.claim: The heavy clouds are cloud masses heavy with water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r17.anchor: سحابا ثقالا } سحائب ثقالا بالماء جمع سحابة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r18.claim: The pronoun in saqnāhu refers grammatically to the masculine word for cloud; taking the clouds by their meaning would call for feminine agreement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r18.anchor: سقناه } الضمير للسحاب على اللفظ ، ولو حمل على المعنى كالثقال لأنث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r19.claim: A dead land is a place without life or one needing irrigation; the phrase means for its watering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r19.anchor: لبلد ميت } لأجل بلد ليس فيه حيا ولسقيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r20.claim: The pronoun in fa-anzalnā bihi can refer to the land, the cloud, or the driving of the cloud.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r20.anchor: فأنزلنا به } بالبلد أو بالسحاب أو بالسوق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r21.claim: The following phrase about bringing out fruit has the same referential possibilities and describes that same bringing forth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r21.anchor: وكذلك { فأخرجنا به . . . } مثل ذلك الإخراج وهو إخراج الثمرات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r22.claim: The two acts of bringing things forth are alike: each restores something after its creation, so reflection should show no difference between them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p105#2/r22.anchor: نخرج الموتى لعلكم تذكرون } فيؤديكم التذكر إلى أنه لا فرق بين الإخراجين

MUJAHID:v1p238#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p238#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p238#3/r1.claim: Bringing the dead out means sending rain until the earth splits open over them.
MUJAHID:v1p238#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد كذلك ﴿ نخرج الموتى ﴾ يعني نمطر السماء حتى تشقق عنهم الأرض

MUQATIL:7:57-58/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r1.claim: The winds are cloud-spreaders; the cited verse says winds stir clouds, which travel ahead of the winds.
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r1.anchor: الرياح نشرا للسحاب، كقوله: يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا [الروم: 48]، يسير السحاب قدام الرياح

MUQATIL:7:57-58/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r2.claim: The wind carries heavy, water-filled clouds to barren land with no vegetation.
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r2.anchor: يعنى إذا حملت الريح { سحابا ثقالا }

MUQATIL:7:57-58/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:57-58/r3.claim: As water brings forth all fruits and plants, God brings the dead out of the earth; this sign calls people to recognize resurrection as certain, as also in al-Rūm and al-Malāʾika.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r1.speaker: مكي وحمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r1.claim: Makki, Hamza, and Ali read the singular الريح instead of plural الرياح.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r2.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r2.claim: Hamza and Ali read بُشْراً as the verbal noun نشروا, governed by أرسل or treated as a circumstantial phrase meaning “spread.”
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r2.anchor: حمزة وعلى مصدر نشروا انتصابه إما لأن أرسل ونشوء متقاربان فكأنه قيل نشرها نشرا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r3.speaker: عاصم
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r3.claim: Asim lightens the reading بشرا, treating it as the plural of بشير because the winds announce rain.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r3.anchor: عاصم تخفيف بشرا تجمع بشير لأن الرياح تبشر بالمطر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r4.speaker: شامي
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r4.claim: The Shami reader lightens نشرًا like the two forms of رسل; the other readers take it as the plural of نشور, winds spreading rain.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r4.anchor: شامى تخفيف نشر كرسل ورسل وهو قراءة الباقين جمع نشور أى ناشرة للمطر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r5.claim: Before God's mercy means before His bounty, namely rain, one of the greatest blessings.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r5.anchor: امام نعمته وهو الغيث الذى هو من أجل النعم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r6.claim: أقلت means the wind-borne clouds carried and raised the water; the derivation relates to قليل, since a lifter regards its burden as small.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r6.anchor: تحملت ورفعت واشتقاق الافلال من القلة لأن الرافع المطيق برى ما يرفعه قليلا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r7.claim: Heavy clouds are loaded with water, and سحاب is the plural/collective of سحابة.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r8.claim: The pronoun in سقناه follows the masculine word form سحاب; following its meaning as a plural would call for feminine agreement, as it would with the adjective ثقيل.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r8.anchor: لانث كما لو حمل الوصف على اللفظ لقيل ثقيلا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r9.speaker: مدني وحمزة وعلى وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r9.claim: The Medinan readers, Hamza, Ali, and Hafs read بلد ميت; the phrase refers to land without rain, brought rain for watering it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r9.anchor: لأجل بلد ليس فيه مطر ولسقيه ميت مدنى وحمزة وعلى وحفص

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r10.claim: The pronoun in أنزلنا به may refer to the cloud or to the driving of the cloud; by the same means fruit is produced.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r10.anchor: بالسحاب أو بالسوق وكذلك ﴿ فأخرجنا به من كل الثمرات

NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r11.claim: Just as God brings out fruits, He brings out the dead; both are renewed after being brought into existence, so reflection leads to belief in resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p16#3/r11.anchor: إذ لا فرق بين الاخراجين لأن كل واحد منهما إعادة الشئ بعد إنشائه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r1.claim: The verse continues the preceding mention of night and day, adds another blessing, and demonstrates God's oneness and divinity.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r1.anchor: عطف على قوله: «يغشي الليل النهار». ذكر شيئا آخر من نعمه، ودل على وحدانيته وثبوت إلهيته.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r2.claim: Riyāḥ is a plural of abundance, arwāḥ a plural of paucity, and rīḥ derives from rūḥ; he rejects aryāḥ as a paucity plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r2.anchor: ورياح جمع كثرة، وأرواح جمع قلة. وأصل ريح روح. وقد خطىء من قال في جمع القلة أرياح.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r3.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r3.claim: They read nushuran with both first syllables rounded, construing it as a plural meaning winds that spread.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r3.anchor: قرأ أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو «نشرا» بضم النون والشين جمع ناشر على معنى النسب، أي ذات نشر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r4.claim: Nushur can also be the plural of nashūr, like rasūl/ rusul; a nashūr wind comes from here and there.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع نشور كرسول ورسل. يقال: ريح النشور إذا أتت من هاهنا وهاهنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r5.claim: Nushūr can mean manshūr, as rakūb means markūb, so the winds are sent out spreading.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r5.anchor: والنشور بمعنى المنشور كالركوب بمعنى المركوب. أي وهو الذي يرسل الرياح منشرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r6.claim: They read nushuran with a rounded nūn and unvoweled shīn, treating it as a softened form of nashara, as in kutub and rusul.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r6.anchor: قرأ الحسن وقتادة «نشرا» بضم النون وإسكان الشين مخففا من نشر كما يقال: كتب ورسل.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r7.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r7.claim: They read nashran with an open nūn and unvoweled shīn as a verbal noun governed by the preceding sense: God spreads the winds.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة «نشرا» بفتح النون وإسكان الشين على المصدر، أعمل فيه معنى ما قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r8.claim: The verbal noun may function circumstantially as life-giving: God sends the winds revivingly, just as one may say someone came running.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا في موضع الحال من الرياح كأنه قال يرسل الرياح منشرة، أي محيية

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r9.claim: On another explanation, the wind is folded while still, then released from its fold and opened when it blows.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r9.anchor: كأن الريح في سكونها كالمطوية ثم ترسل من طيها ذلك فتصير كالمنفتحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r10.claim: He glosses nashran as dispersed in their directions, sent here and there.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r10.anchor: وقد فسره أبو عبيد بمعنى متفرقة في وجوهها، على معنى ينشرها ها هنا وها هنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r11.speaker: عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r11.claim: He reads bushran with bāʾ and a still shīn, a plural of bashīr: winds give glad tidings of rain, supported by 30:46.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r11.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: «بشرا» بالباء وإسكان الشين والتنوين جمع بشير، أي الرياح تبشر بالمطر.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r12.claim: The shīn in this reading is originally rounded but made still for ease, like the forms rusul and rusl.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r12.anchor: وأصل الشين الضم، لكن سكنت تخفيفا كرسل ورسل.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r13.speaker: عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r13.claim: A transmitted version from him opens the bāʾ; al-Naḥḥās also reports bushr and bashar as verbal nouns from giving glad tidings.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r13.anchor: وروى عنه «بشرا» بفتح الباء. قال النحاس: ويقرأ «بشرا» و«بشر مصدر بشره

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r14.speaker: محمد اليماني
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r14.claim: He reads bushrā on the pattern of ḥublā.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r14.anchor: وقرأ محمد اليماني «بشرى» على وزن حبلى.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r15.claim: A seventh reading has bushrā with both bāʾ and shīn rounded.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r16.claim: Saḥāb may be grammatically masculine or feminine, like other collective nouns whose singular ends in tāʾ marbūṭa, and it can take either adjective form.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r16.anchor: السحاب يذكر ويؤنث. وكذا كل جمع بينه وبين واحدته هاء. ويجوز نعته بواحد فتقول: سحاب ثقيل وثقيلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r17.claim: The wind carries clouds heavy with water; aqallat means that it bore them, since aqalla means to carry something.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r17.anchor: حملت الريح سحابا ثقالا بالماء، أي أثقلت بحمله. يقال: أقل فلان الشيء أي حمله.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r18.claim: In saqnāhu, the pronoun refers to the clouds.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r18.anchor: يقال: أقل فلان الشيء أي حمله. { سقناه } أي السحاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r19.claim: A dead land is a place without vegetation; one may say the cloud was driven to or toward a place, and the lām may express purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57/r19.anchor: { لبلد ميت } أي ليس فيه نبات. يقال: سقته لبلد كذا وإلى بلد كذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r1.claim: The cited line uses ablād in a poem about decay covering traces.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r1.anchor: من بعد ما شمل البلى أبلادها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r2.claim: Balad can also mean an ostrich nest; the idiom about the ostrich egg describes an egg the bird abandons.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r2.anchor: والبلد: أدحي النعام. يقال: هو أذل من بيضة البلد، أي من بيضة النعام التي يتركها.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r3.claim: Balda can mean land, as in saying this is our land just as one says our sea.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r3.anchor: والبلدة الأرض يقال: هذه بلدتنا كما يقال بحرتنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r4.claim: Balda is also a lunar mansion of six stars in Sagittarius, where the sun arrives on the year's shortest day.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r4.anchor: والبلدة من منازل القمر، وهي ستة أنجم من القوس تنزلها الشمس في أقصر يوم في السنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:57#2/r5.claim: Balda can mean the chest; the poem describes a camel kneeling and lowering its chest to the ground.
