WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says النشر describes the pleasant, gentle winds that form clouds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: (النشر من الرياح الطيبة اللينة التي تنشئ السحاب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī gives نشور as the singular and connects نشر to pleasant fragrance; the author cites an Imruʾ al-Qays poem as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p185/r9.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (واحدها نشور، وأصل هذا من النشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses نشرا as winds dispersed from every direction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ({نشرا} أي: متفرقة من كل جانب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r2.claim: Abū Bakr glosses the winds as spread out and broad in their blowing; نشر means dispersal, as in spreading cloth or sawing wood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر: (هي المنتشرة الواسعة الهبوب، والنشر: التفريق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r3.claim: The reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī can be parsed by ellipsis as ذوات نشر, meaning fragrant winds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: {نشرا} يجوز أن يكون من باب حذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “before His mercy” means before the rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: بين يدي المطر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses it as ahead of His rain.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq takes the phrase as before the rain, which is God’s mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r6.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي: بين يدي المطر الذي هو رحمته)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r7.claim: Abū Bakr explains “the hands of” metaphorically as precedence: Arabs say trials are before the Hour, and winds precede and signal rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p188/r7.anchor: اليدان تستعملهما العرب في المجاز على معنى التقدمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r1.claim: Aqalla means to carry, as does istaqalla; the winds carry clouds heavy with water, according to the exegetes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r1.anchor: يقال: أقل فلان الشيء أي (¬5) حمله، وكذلك استقله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r2.claim: Sahāb is grammatically masculine although it is a collective form of sahāba, like tamr/tamra and jawz/jawza; this explains the masculine pronoun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r2.anchor: والسحاب لفظه مذكر وإن كان جمع سحابة، لذلك ذكر الكناية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a dead land is one without vegetation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: ليس فيه نبات)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says it is a place where nothing grows.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r5.claim: Abū Bakr explains the cloud is driven to a place needing rain because rain has ceased there; the lām can mean “toward” or “for the sake of.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r5.anchor: وقال أبو بكر: (أي: سقنا السحاب لبلد وإلى بلد محتاج إلى المطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r6.claim: A balad is any part of earth, settled or unsettled, empty or inhabited; its subdivision is a baldah, plural bilād, and wilderness can also be called baldah. Al-Aʿshā’s line uses بلد for a desolate wilderness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p189/r6.anchor: وأما البلد فكل موضع من الأرض عامر أو غير عامر خال أو مسكون فهو بلد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r1.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Anbārī say “We sent down water by it” can mean by the land or by the cloud, since cloud is the instrument for sending down water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج وابن الأنباري (¬2): (جائز أن يكون فأنزلنا بالبلد الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r2.claim: The apparent referent of the pronoun in “by it We brought forth” is water, because fruit is brought out by water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r2.anchor: الظاهر أن الكناية تعود إلى الماء؛ لأن إخراج الثمرات كان بالماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj also permits taking the pronoun as the land, since the passage does not specify one particular land.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (وجائز أن يكون فأخرجنا بالبلد من كل الثمرات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r4.claim: The resurrection of the dead is likened to bringing forth plants from the dead land.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {كذلك نخرج الموتى} أي: مثل ذلك الإخراج الذي أشرنا إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r5.claim: Abū Bakr makes the analogy explicit: reviving the dead after they have become remains in the soil is like reviving earth with vegetation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p191/r5.anchor: وقال أبو بكر: (أي: نحيي الموتى مثل ذلك الإحياء الذي وصفناه في البلد الميت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “so that you may remember” as “so that you may take admonition.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the evidence should lead people to infer God’s oneness and resurrection; laʿalla expresses hope from the human addressees’ perspective, since God knows whether they will heed it and people speak according to what they know and hope from others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p192/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (أي: لعلكم بما بينا (¬2) لكم تستدلون على توحيد الله

ASAD-NOTES:7:57#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:57#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:57#n44/r1.claim: The parable's key point is that the power that makes plants grow will resurrect the dead at the end of time.
ASAD-NOTES:7:57#n44/r1.anchor: by the exercise of the same life-giving power by which God causes plants to grow, He will resurrect the dead at the end of time.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r4.claim: The phrase describing winds as nushuran means pleasant and gentle, from nashr in the sense of a pleasant scent.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r4.anchor: طيبة لينة، من النشر وهو الرائحة الطيبة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes the winds as scattered in every direction, meaning dispersed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r5.anchor: وقيل: متفرقة في كل جانب، بمعنى المنتشرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r6.claim: Before God's mercy means before the rain; the winds lift clouds heavy with water and drive them to a land without vegetation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r6.anchor: قدام مطره { حتى إذا أقلت } أي: حملت هذه الرياح { سحابا ثقالا } بما فيها من الماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r7.claim: God sends down water in the dead land and brings out every kind of fruit through that water.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r7.anchor: فأنزلنا به } بذلك البلد { الماء فأخرجنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r8.claim: Bringing the dead to life resembles reviving the dead land; the sign should prompt reflection on God's oneness and power to resurrect.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:56-57/r8.anchor: نحيي الموتى مثل ذلك الإحياء الذي وصفناه في البلد الميت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r1.claim: For nisba to a collective broken plural, Sībawayh generally derives from its singular form, distinguishing a collective plural from a form used as one name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r1.anchor: إذا أضفت إلى جميع أبدا فإنك توقع الإضافة على واحده الذي كسر ~~عليه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r2.claim: Tribal and collective examples include قبلي, قبلية, بنوي, and ربي, with nisba formed from the corresponding singular base.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r2.anchor: قول العرب في رجل من القبائل قبلي وقبلية للمرأة ومن ذلك أيضا ~~قولهم في أبناء فارس بنوي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r3.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r3.claim: Yūnus analyzes الرباب as the plural of ربة, like جفرة/جفار and علبة/علاب, and glosses ربة as a group of people.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r3.anchor: وقال يونس إنما هي ربة ورباب كقولك ~~جفرة وجفار وعلبة وعلاب والربة الفرقة من الناس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r4.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl explains مسمعي and مهلبي by saying المسامعة and المهالبة have no singular form used as an individual name.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r4.anchor: وزعم الخليل أن نحو ذلك قولهم في المسامعة مسمعي والمهالبة مهلبي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r5.claim: Nisba to نفر and رهط is نفري and رهطي because these collectives have no broken singular; نفر is like حجر in this respect.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r5.anchor: وتقول في الإضافة إلى ~~نفر نفري ورهط رهطي لأن نفر بمنزلة حجر لم يكسر له واحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r6.claim: For أناس he gives إنساني and أناسي, preferring this analysis because أناس has no broken singular إنسان.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r6.anchor: وتقول في الإضافة إلى أناس إنساني وأناسي لأنه ~~لم يكسر له إنسان وهو أجود القولين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r7.claim: Abū Zayd gives محاسني for nisba to محاسن because it has no singular, making it like نفر.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r7.anchor: وقال أبو زيد النسبة إلى محاسن محاسني ~~لأنه لا واحد له فصار بمنزلة نفر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r8.claim: نساء takes نسوي because نسوة is a collective, not a broken plural of a singular; أنفار likewise yields نفري, like أنباط/نبطي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r8.anchor: وتقول في الإضافة إلى نساء نسوي لأنه ~~جماع نسوة وليس نسوة بجمع كسر له واحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r9.claim: For عباديد, which has no singular, he uses عباديدي and cautions against inventing a singular pattern before it is attested.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r9.anchor: وإن أضفت إلى عباديد قلت عباديدي لأنه ليس له واحد ~~وواحده يكون على فعلول أو فعليل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r10.claim: الأعراب takes أعرابي because it lacks a singular with the same meaning; العرب does not have that meaning.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r10.anchor: أعرابي لأنه ليس له واحد على هذا المعنى ألا ترى أنك تقول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r11.claim: When the plural form is itself a personal name, nisba preserves it, as in أنماري and كلابي; a name ضربات similarly gives ضربي without changing its internal vowel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r11.anchor: ~~قالوا في أنمار أنماري لأن أنمارا اسم رجل وقالوا في كلاب كلابي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r12.claim: مدائني treats the pattern مدائن as a place name for purposes of nisba.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r12.anchor: وسألته عن قولهم مدائني فقال صار هذا البناء عندهم اسما ~~لبلد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r13.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r13.speaker: بنو سعد
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r13.claim: Banū Saʿd say أبناوي for أبناء, treating it as the name of a clan, like a place name and a collective singular.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r13.anchor: ومن ثم قالت بنو سعد في الأبناء أبناوي كأنهم جعلوه اسم الحي والحي ~~كالبلد وهو واحد يقع على الجميع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r14.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r14.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r14.claim: He records ضبابي when الضباب is a man's name, معافري for معافر, and أنصاري for الأنصار; معافر is said to be Tamīm's brother.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىالجمع)#577/r14.anchor: وقالوا في الضباب إذا كان اسم رجل ضبابي وفي معافر معافري وهو ~~فيما يزعمون معافر بن مر أخو تميم بن مر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p632/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p632/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p632/r1.claim: The Qur’an commonly uses plural al-riyāḥ for beneficial winds that herald good, citing examples in al-Baqara, al-Ḥijr, al-Jāthiya, and al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p632/r1.anchor: أما كلمة الرياح فهي تستعمل في القرآن الكريم للخير كالرياح المبشّرات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p789/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p789/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p789/r1.claim: Present-tense verbs can stage past events vividly as if before the listener; the verse uses this present-tense scene for sending winds and bringing out the dead.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p789/r1.anchor: الأحداث الماضية بأفعال مضارعة؛ حكاية الحال تُعبّر عن حدث ماضي بفعل مضارع كأنما نريد أن نستحضر الحدث أمامنا

NASHR:v2p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p223/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in all the listed forms of «الميتة/ميتا», «بلد ميت», and «الحي من الميت والميت من الحي».
NASHR:v2p223/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء في جميع ذلك، ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة

AZRAQI:v1p138/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r1.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r1.claim: The account describes a ten-cubit-high structure approached by marble steps and an enclosing wall extending two hundred cubits around the Qullays.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r1.anchor: عشرة أذرع في السماء وكان يصعد عليه بدرج الرخام وحوله سور بينه وبين القليس مايتا ذراع

AZRAQI:v1p138/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r2.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r2.claim: Its twenty-cubit stonework used tightly fitted engraved stones called al-jurub, colored triangular courses, and projecting rounded beams of sasam wood.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r2.anchor: بحجارة تسميها أهل اليمن الجروب منقوشة مطابقة لا يدخل بين أطباقها الإبرة مطبقة به وجعل طول ما بنى به

AZRAQI:v1p138/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r3.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r3.claim: The exterior had a carved marble frieze and gleaming black, yellow, and white stones; its wall was six cubits wide, though its overall length and width were not remembered.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r3.anchor: وكان عرض حايط القليس ستة أذرع وذكروا أنهم لا يحفظون ذرع طول القليس ولا عرضه

AZRAQI:v1p138/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r4.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r4.claim: A ten-by-four-cubit copper door opened into an eighty-by-forty-cubit chamber with ornamented teak work and gold and silver nails.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r4.anchor: وكان له باب من نحاس عشرة أذرع طولا في أربعة أذرع عرضا وكان المدخل منه إلى بيت في جوفه طوله ثمانون ذراعا

AZRAQI:v1p138/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r5.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r5.claim: The chamber led to a forty-cubit portico whose arches bore tree-patterned mosaics and visible gold stars.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r5.anchor: ثم يدخل من البيت إلى إيوان طوله أربعون ذراعا عن يمينه وعن يساره وعقوده مضروبة بالفسيفساء مشجرة

AZRAQI:v1p138/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r6.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r6.claim: The portico led to a thirty-by-thirty-cubit dome decorated with mosaic crosses and a polished, square panel of striped stone on its eastern side.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r6.anchor: ثم يدخل من الإيوان إلى قبة ثلاثون ذراعا في ثلاثين ذراعا جدرهما بالفسيفساء وفيها صلب منقوشة بالفسيفساء والذهب

AZRAQI:v1p138/r7.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r7.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r7.claim: The eastern panel transmitted sunlight and moonlight into the dome; beneath it stood a labakh-wood pulpit with ivory and teak steps decorated in gold and silver.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r7.anchor: تؤدي ضوء الشمس والقمر إلى داخل القبة وكان تحت الرخامة منبر من خشب اللبخ وهو عندهم الأبنوس

AZRAQI:v1p138/r8.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r8.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r8.claim: Silver chains hung in the dome, and two long carved teak beams called Kaʿib and Imraʾat Kaʿib were venerated in pre-Islamic times; Kaʿib was also called al-Ahwazi, said to mean free.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r8.anchor: وكان في القبة سلاسل فضة وكان في القبة أو في البيت خشبة ساج منقوشة طولها ستون ذراعا يقال لها كعيب

AZRAQI:v1p138/r9.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p138/r9.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v1p138/r9.claim: Abraha drove the builders harshly, swearing to cut off the hand of any worker caught idle at sunset.
AZRAQI:v1p138/r9.anchor: وكان أبرهة عند بناء القليس قد أخذ العمال بالعمل أخذا شديدا وكان آلى أن لا تطلع الشمس على عامل لم يضع يده

AZRAQI:v1p322/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p322/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
AZRAQI:v1p322/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says both the Black Stone and the Maqām are from Paradise.

AZRAQI:v1p322/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p322/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p322/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Black Stone and Maqām are the only objects from Paradise on earth; had polytheists not touched them, the afflicted would be healed by touching them.
AZRAQI:v1p322/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال ليس في الأرض من الجنة إلا الركن الأسود والمقام

AZRAQI:v1p322/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p322/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
AZRAQI:v1p322/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says pagan impurities keep the Black Stone from healing the afflicted, and that it descended whiter than silver.
AZRAQI:v1p322/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص نزل الركن وأنه لأشد بياضا من الفضة

AZRAQI:v1p322/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p322/r4.speaker: النبي
AZRAQI:v1p322/r4.claim: The Prophet tells Aisha that the Black Stone was a white ruby from Paradise; pagan sins altered and veiled its beauty, though it would otherwise heal every illness and be restored to its first state.
AZRAQI:v1p322/r4.anchor: أن النبي & قال لعائشة وهي تطوف معه بالكعبة حين استلم الركن لولا ما طبع على هذا الحجر يا عائشة

AZRAQI:v1p322/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p322/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
AZRAQI:v1p322/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says God will resurrect the Black Stone with eyes and a speaking tongue to testify for those who rightly touch it.
AZRAQI:v1p322/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي & قال إن الله عز وجل يبعث الركن الأسود له عينان يبصر بهما ولسان ينطق به

AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the sanctuary initially had no enclosing wall; surrounding houses and their doorways gave access from every side.
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال كان المسجد الحرام ليس عليه جدرات محاطة إنما كانت الدور محدقة به من كل جانب

AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r2.claim: Crowding leads Umar to buy and demolish neighboring houses, place contested purchase money in the Kaaba treasury, and enclose the mosque with a low wall; he says those houses adjoin the Kaaba's courtyard, not vice versa.
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r2.anchor: فاشترى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه دورا فهدمها وهدم على من قرب من المسجد وأبى بعضهم أن يأخذ الثمن

AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r3.claim: When Uthman expands the mosque, some owners protest demolition; he cites Umar's precedent, imprisons them, then releases them after Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Asid intercedes.
AZRAQI:v2p68#2/r3.anchor: ثم كثر الناس في زمن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه فوسع المسجد واشترى من قوم وأبى آخرون أن يبيعوا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r1.claim: By استعارة, رحمة in the wind-and-rain verse means rain; خزائن رحمة and opened mercy mean stores of provision and provision granted.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r1.anchor: وقد توضع (الرحمة) موضع (المطر) لأنه ينزل برحمته.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r1.claim: The disbelievers’ claim that time alone destroys them is false literal assertion, not metaphor, because they state it ignorantly rather than interpretively.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r1.anchor: من حيث لم يتكلم به قائله على انه متاول بل اطلقه بجهله وعماه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r2.claim: A clause is metaphorical when interpretation deliberately moves its judgment from its rational place, as in assigning an act to spring, a cause rather than the agent.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r2.anchor: كل جملة أخرجت الحكم المفاد بها عن موضوعه في العقل لضرب من التأول فهي مجاز

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r3.claim: The Qur’an attributes fruiting, increased faith, and release of earthly burdens to trees, verses, and earth as causes; the actual agent is God.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r3.anchor: تؤتى أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r4.claim: These attributions are interpretive: trees do not produce fruit, verses do not create knowledge, nor earth disclose its contents unaided; God sets the movement that reveals what He placed there.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p332/r4.anchor: ولكن إذا حدثت فيها الحركة بقدرة الله ظهر ما كنز فيها واودع جوفها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r1.claim: A bare statement that someone reads without understanding gains force when followed by a verse and a poetic illustration that makes the point vivid.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r1.anchor: أن تقول فلان يكد نفسه في قراءة الكتب ولا يفهم منها شيئا وتسكت وبين أن تتلو الآية وتنشد قول الشاعر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r2.claim: Images of leafy but fruitless trees and green bitter wood make the contrast between attractive appearance and poor substance unfold vividly.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r2.anchor: وانظر إلى المعنى في الحالة الثانية كيف يورق شجره ويثمر ويفتر ثغره ويبسم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r3.claim: Ibn Lankak’s image makes a handsome person’s ugly conduct seem to disfigure his appearance, intensifying the rebuke through representation.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r3.anchor: إذا أخو الحسن أضحى فعله سمجا رأيت صورته من أقبح الصور

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r4.claim: Abū Tammām’s second line completes the image: slander is like fire whose heat reveals agarwood’s fragrance, exposing and enhancing a hidden virtue.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r4.anchor: وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r5.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s bitter-mouth simile rebukes and restrains the ignorant more powerfully than directly stating that corrupt judgment mistakes right for wrong.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p99/r5.anchor: ومن يك ذا فم مر مريض يجد مرا به الماء الزلالا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r1.claim: With a subject-first question, the event is already known and the question asks who performed it; a verb-first question asks whether the event occurred, so the forms cannot be exchanged freely.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r1.anchor: وإنما شككت في الفاعل من هو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r2.claim: A generic question such as whether anyone ever spoke poetry asks about occurrence, not identity; asking whether this person did so is ill-formed without a particular known event whose agent is in doubt.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r2.anchor: لا معنى للسؤال عن الفاعل من هو في مثل هذا ، لأن ذلك إنما يتصور إذا كانت الإشارة إلى فعل مخصوص

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r3.claim: The same distinction applies when the hamza seeks confirmation: the Qur'anic question to Abraham asks him to confirm that he was the agent who acted against the idols.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p100/r3.anchor: أأنت فعلت هذا بآلهتنا يا إبراهيم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r1.claim: Rīḥ is moving air; rūḥ is a breeze, and arīḥī describes a generous or expansive character.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r1.anchor: الريح : الهواء المتحرك . والروح نسيم الريح . والأريحي : الواسع الخلق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r2.claim: Rīḥ can mean the wind itself.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p316/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الريح في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : -

BURHAN:v1p130/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p130/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p130/r1.claim: Al-Aʿrāf has سقناه لبلد ميت, while Fāṭir changes the preposition to إلى.
BURHAN:v1p130/r1.anchor: في الأعراف ﴿ سقناه لبلد ميت ﴾ وفي فاطر ﴿ إلى بلد ﴾

BURHAN:v3p356/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p356/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p356/r1.claim: Plural forms conventionally associated with a small count can denote abundance; the Qur'an supplies many examples, including الصابرين والصادقين and المؤمنين والمؤمنات.
BURHAN:v3p356/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ من كل الثمرات ﴾ 2 ﴿ إن تبدوا الصدقات ﴾ 3 ﴿ الصابرين والصادقين ﴾ 4 الآية

BURHAN:v4p318/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p318/r1.claim: كل may be emphatic, introduced as an annexed topic, or detached from annexation; non-emphatic كل normally attaches to an indefinite generic to convey comprehensive coverage.
BURHAN:v4p318/r1.anchor: مؤكدة ومبتدأ بها مضافة ومقطوعة عن الإضافة

BURHAN:v4p318/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p318/r2.claim: Attaching كل to a definite noun is usually awkward outside a subject with a single-word predicate, but it works when the article is generic, as in من كل الثمرات.
BURHAN:v4p318/r2.anchor: فإن لم يكن مبتدأ وأضفته إلى جملة معرفة نحو ضربت كل إخوتك وضربت كل القوم

BURHAN:v4p318/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r3.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p318/r3.claim: Al-Suhayli explains that من marks genus, not partitive division, and its phrase is the object; placing كل first prevents the genitive phrase from being mistaken for an adverbial source.
BURHAN:v4p318/r3.anchor: قال السهيلي في النتائج ( 2 ) له حكمة وهو إن من في الآية لبيان الجنس

BURHAN:v4p318/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p318/r4.claim: If كل came after الثمرات, readers might treat من الثمرات as an adverbial phrase and seek the object of أخرجنا afterward; fronting كل signals coverage of the generic class.
BURHAN:v4p318/r4.anchor: ولو قال أخرجنا به من الثمرات كلها لقيل أي شيء أخرج منها وذهب التوهم إلى إن المجرور في موضع ظرف

BURHAN:v4p318/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p318/r6.claim: Putting كل before the generic phrase indicates coverage of the whole class, while placing it after can emphasize the entire already specified set, whether generic or definite.
BURHAN:v4p318/r6.anchor: إذا تقدمت اقتضت الإحاطة بالجنس وإذا تأخرت اقتضت الإحاطة بالمؤكد بتمامه جنسا شائعا

DAMGHANI:v1p93/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r4.claim: Thiqāl can mean things heavy with water and a woman heavy with a child, meaning her pregnancy has become apparent.
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r4.anchor: السادس الثقل بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف سحابا ثقالا سقناه يعني ثقالا بالماء فيها مثلها فلما أثقلت

DAMGHANI:v1p445/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r3.claim: A dead land is land without vegetation; other examples describe its revival through plants.
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r3.anchor: الثالث : الميت والميتة قلة النبات . قوله سبحانه في سورة الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p201/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p201/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p201/r7.claim: A fourth sense is a place without vegetation, glossed as dead land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p201/r7.anchor: والرابع : المكان الذي لا نبت فيه ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r6.claim: Mawt can describe drought or barren land; every dead land in the Qur’an means uncultivated earth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p569/r6.anchor: الرابع : الجدب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r5.claim: A Qur'anic sense of ثقل is heaviness, including heavy clouds and a pregnant woman becoming heavy.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الثقل في القرآن على عشرة أوجه
